Interim fix from ADR-006's alternatives -- independent of the auth work and strictly less effort. Do this now regardless of whether the public-origin path is ever taken.

SPAXEL_ADVERTISED_BASE_URL is http://10.20.23.203:8080 and the node's NVS has ms_ip=10.20.23.203. That address is k3s-agent-minisforum, where the pod happens to run because the Deployment uses hostNetwork: true. Nothing pins it there. If it reschedules, both the OTA download URL and every provisioned node's mothership address break silently -- the node just stops connecting, with no indication why.

k8s/ardenone-cluster/spaxel/deployment.yml already carries this caveat in its own hostNetwork comment ('Node IP is currently 10.20.23.203 (k3s-agent-minisforum) -- will change if this pod is ever scheduled elsewhere, since nothing pins it to that node'). It was written as a known risk and never closed.

Change: add a nodeSelector (or node affinity) pinning the Deployment to k3s-agent-minisforum, and update the comment to say the IP is now durable rather than incidental.

Consider also whether a LAN-resolvable DNS name would be better than an IP -- it would survive a deliberate move, where a nodeSelector just relocates the problem. Either is better than the status quo.

Acceptance: the pod cannot be scheduled off k3s-agent-minisforum; deleting the pod reschedules it to the same node and 10.20.23.203:8080 still answers.
issue.title: Pin the spaxel pod to a node so the LAN OTA base URL stays valid

issue.description:
ADR-008 decision 5. GATES all PKI identity work. This is a measurement with a number attached, not a formality -- a bad result is allowed to send us back to the ADR-007 symmetric design.

Why: RAM is the binding constraint for certificate-based identity, and the TLS path has NEVER actually executed on this hardware. wss:// support shipped in 0.2.19, but the deployed config uses plain ws:// on the LAN (ADR-006 decision 6), so no handshake has run alongside WiFi + NimBLE + CSI. There is no measured peak-heap figure, and mTLS RAISES it -- a client key operation plus a second chain on top of server verification.

Measured statics on the current build (for reference, these are fine):
  IRAM      97,358 B (26.9% used)
  D/IRAM    59,604 B (17.2% used), 286,252 B remaining at link
  flash     1,684,597 B of 2,031,616 B slot, 346,912 B (17%) free

Two pieces of work:

1. Enable CONFIG_SPIRAM. The chip has 2MB PSRAM sitting unused -- esptool flash-id reports "Embedded PSRAM 2MB (AP_3v3)" and sdkconfig has "# CONFIG_SPIRAM is not set". This is the single biggest lever and it is config-only. Validate it ON ITS OWN, not bundled with identity work: it changes allocator placement and DMA constraints globally.

2. Surface and record free heap. The firmware already sends free_heap_bytes in its status message (websocket.c:494) and the mothership already has a free_heap_bytes column (db/migrations.go:258) -- it is simply not exposed by any API response. Surface it, then force a real TLS connection (point a node at the 443 path) and capture the peak.

Deliverable: measured free heap at idle and at TLS handshake peak, with and without PSRAM. Then an explicit go/no-go on whether mTLS client certs fit.

If NO-GO: say so plainly and fall back to ADR-007 symmetric, which is strictly cheaper in both flash and heap. ADR-008 records that this outcome is allowed.

issue.description:
mothership/internal/explainability/handler.go refreshData() (POST /api/explain/refresh handler, ~line 323-341), Component 28 Detection Explainability (docs/plan/plan.md ~line 2021-2043), sets the stored fusion result snapshot timestamp like this:

    h.fusionResult = &FusionResultSnapshot{
        Timestamp: int64(req.GridData.Rows), // placeholder
        Blobs:     req.Blobs,
        GridData:  req.GridData,
    }

req.GridData.Rows is the accumulation grid's row COUNT (a small integer, e.g. tens to low hundreds -- a dimension, not a time), not a Unix timestamp. Whatever consumes FusionResultSnapshot.Timestamp downstream (staleness checks, "why is this here" explanation ordering/display, any freshness comparison against real wall-clock time) receives a value that resolves to a date near the Unix epoch (1970) rather than the actual refresh time -- silently wrong, not merely imprecise.

No open or in-progress bead currently tracks this specific line (distinct from the GDOP-improvement placeholder bf-68vvo and the other in-progress placeholder beads already filed -- checked title/description text of all open+in-progress beads, none reference GridData.Rows or this handler).

Fix: replace with an actual timestamp -- time.Now().UnixMilli() (matching the Unix-milliseconds convention used elsewhere in this plan/codebase, e.g. the WebSocket JSON message schemas' timestamp_ms fields) at the point refreshData receives the POST, unless the caller (dashboard) is expected to supply its own capture timestamp in the request body, in which case add a Timestamp field to the request struct and thread it through instead of fabricating one. Check how FusionResultSnapshot.Timestamp is actually consumed (grep explainability package + dashboard/js callers of /api/explain) to pick the correct one. Add/adjust a unit test in mothership/internal/explainability asserting the stored Timestamp is a plausible current-time value (e.g. within a few seconds of time.Now()), not derived from grid dimensions. Verify with: cd mothership && go test ./internal/explainability/... -v.
issue.title: Explainability refreshData sets Timestamp from GridData.Rows instead of an actual time (meaningless value)

     Host(`spaxel.ardenone.com`) && (PathPrefix(`/ws/node`) || PathPrefix(`/healthz`) || PathPrefix(`/api/provision`))

Acceptance: an authenticated node OTAs successfully with the base URL set to the public origin; an unauthenticated curl to /firmware/... gets 404 (not an OAuth redirect, and not a binary).

issue.description:
Umbrella for defects found during the **first on-hardware validation of firmware/** (2026-07-28). Until this date the ESP32-S3 firmware had never been compiled or run against real hardware: CI (`spaxel-build`) only builds the mothership Docker image, and `docs/notes/firmware-host-test-approach.md` records that ESP-IDF was not even installed on the host that made the host-test decision. All PROGRESS.md validation to date is simulator-driven (`cmd/sim`), which by construction cannot exercise `firmware/main/*`.

What was verified on hardware:
- Target board: ESP32-S3 (QFN56) rev v0.2, 4 MB embedded flash + 2 MB PSRAM, native USB-Serial/JTAG only (USB ID 303a:1001), no USB-UART bridge present.
- `firmware/` compiles clean under ESP-IDF v5.2 (5 cosmetic warnings only). App binary 1,631,552 bytes — fits the 0x1F0000 factory partition with ~20% free.
- The firmware **boots and runs**: NVS schema migration, MAC read, config load, provisioning window, WiFi init, mDNS (`spaxel-node.local`), LED init, BLE init + scan, captive portal AP `spaxel-3DC8` with DHCP on 192.168.4.1. No panic, no boot loop.

So the firmware is far healthier than "never compiled" would suggest — but three functional defects were exposed that no simulator run could have caught, plus the process gap that let them sit unnoticed. Children of this bead cover each.

Closes when all children are closed and a node has been observed streaming CSI frames to a live mothership.

issue.description:
GET /api/occupancy (mothership/internal/api/status.go, getOccupancy handler at line 122, TODO at line 151) always returns an empty "people" array for every zone: `People: []string{}, // TODO: resolve blob IDs to person labels`. It never converts occupied blob IDs to BLE-identified person names, even though BLE-to-blob identity matching (Component 21/Component 9 in docs/plan/plan.md, implemented in mothership/internal/ble -- see IdentityMatch.PersonName in internal/ble/identity.go) is already built and populates person names elsewhere (e.g. the dashboard snapshot's blobs[].person field, plan.md ~line 903-904 and ~908-909 "people": ["Alice"]). The plan's documented occupancy/zone snapshot explicitly includes real names, and mothership/internal/api/status.go's own doc comment on occupancyResponse says "people: List of person names (BLE-identified) in the zone" -- but the implementation never does this lookup, so /api/occupancy (and anything consuming it, e.g. Simple Mode room cards per plan.md Component 8d ~line 1010 "Shows occupancy count, person names... and status color") is silently wrong: it will always show 0 named people even when BLE identity is confidently resolved.

Root closed bead bf-59me3 ("GET /api/status and GET /api/occupancy endpoints") shipped the endpoint shape but left this specific resolution as a stub; no open bead currently tracks finishing it.

Fix: in getOccupancy (mothership/internal/api/status.go), wire an identity-resolution provider (mirroring how other subsystems already consume mothership/internal/ble's identity matches/tracker -- grep for existing consumers of ble.IdentityMatch or a "identity provider" interface already wired into StatusHandler's siblings, e.g. how internal/analytics/alert_handler.go or the dashboard snapshot builder gets person names for blobs) so that for each zone, People is populated with the PersonName (or Label(), once bf-5mx46 lands) of each BLE-identified blob currently inside that zone, falling back to omitting unidentified blobs from the People list (they still count toward Count). Add/extend a unit test in mothership/internal/api/status_test.go covering: a zone with one BLE-identified occupant returns that person's name in People; a zone with an unidentified blob returns Count>0 but People=[]. Verify with: cd ~/spaxel/mothership && go test ./internal/api/... -run Occupancy -v.
issue.notes:

- resolvePeopleIDs() method that converts blob IDs to person names, handling deduplication and unidentified blobs
- Full wiring in main.go via bleIdentityAdapter (line 4583)
- Comprehensive unit tests covering BLE-identified occupants, unidentified blobs, nil provider, multiple people (with deduplication), and mixed identity scenarios

issue.description:
ADR-007 phase 3. Sizing work first -- this may not fit.

Two separate things:

1. Flash encryption (CONFIG_SECURE_FLASH_ENC_ENABLED, currently not set). Makes an NVS dump useless. Most valuable during phase 1 while the per-device key still lives in NVS, but it is an irreversible eFuse burn, so it trades one risk for another. Consider also CONFIG_SECURE_ROM_DL_MODE_ENABLED, currently y -- disabling or restricting ROM download mode closes the esptool read path that was used to extract the credential on 2026-08-07, at the cost of making recovery harder on a rig where recovery is already unreliable (bf-4z6wh).

2. Secure Boot v2 (CONFIG_SECURE_BOOT, currently not set; CONFIG_SECURE_BOOT_V2_RSA_SUPPORTED=y and CONFIG_SECURE_BOOT_V2_PREFERRED=y so the hardware is willing). This is what closes the HMAC_UP oracle limitation from phase 2 -- without it, hostile firmware on the device can ask the peripheral to sign anything.

THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IS BOOTLOADER SIZE. docs/notes/esp32-ota-and-reconnection-handoff.md measured only ~11,056 bytes free in the bootloader, and Secure Boot v2 signature verification is not free. Measure before promising this: the current build reports Bootloader binary size 0x51b0 with 0x2e50 (36%) free, so the headroom is real but tight.

Start with a sizing spike and a written go/no-go, not an implementation. If it does not fit, the honest outcome is that phase 2 proves THIS CHIP but not WHICH FIRMWARE, and that limitation is documented in ADR-007 rather than quietly assumed away.

Acceptance: a measured report of bootloader size with Secure Boot v2 enabled, a go/no-go, and if go, a staged rollout plan that accounts for the burns being irreversible.
issue.title: Phase 3: size and enable flash encryption + Secure Boot v2

issue.description:
## Problem

`js/viz3d.js` declares `_renderer` twice:

- Line 13: `let _scene, _camera, _controls, _clock, _renderer;`
- Line 30: `let _renderer = null;`

This throws `SyntaxError: Identifier '_renderer' has already been declared` when the dashboard loads, killing the entire Viz3D IIFE. The cascade failure is what causes the home page's overlapping-panels visual chaos (Playwright review 2026-04-24).

## Fix

Delete line 30 of `js/viz3d.js`. Initialize `_renderer` in the existing declaration on line 13, or leave the declaration and assign later — whichever is consistent with how other private module state is handled in that file.

## Verification

1. Load the dashboard home page; open DevTools console.
2. Confirm no `SyntaxError: Identifier '_renderer' has already been declared`.
3. Confirm `Viz3D` global is defined (`typeof Viz3D === 'object'`).
4. Run existing unit tests: `cd dashboard && npm test` (Jest suite covers viz3d).

issue.description:
Split from bf-2eub9 (umbrella). CHILD 1 of the bf-2eub9 chain. Apply the root-cause fix pinned by bf-20q9o (closed) so spaxel-sim's CSI stops being dropped before it reaches Fuse.

## Root cause (from bf-20q9o)
CSIFrame.LinkID() (mothership/internal/ingestion/frame.go:119-121) joins the two MACs with ':' -> "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:11:22:33:44:55:66" (colon-joined, NO dash). splitLinkID (mothership/cmd/mothership/main.go:5421) scanned only for '-' and returned nil for every link, so gatherFusionLinks returned an empty slice -> Fuse([]) -> 0 peaks -> 0 blobs. Both blob paths are broken identically (2D localizer at main.go:2786 uses the same splitLinkID).

## Task
Land the splitLinkID fix already drafted in the working tree: a fixed-width split (each MAC is exactly 17 chars "XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX"; canonical two-MAC form is 35 chars with the boundary at index 17) that handles BOTH the actual colon-joined producer format AND the documented dash format, keeping the '-' scan as a defensive fallback. This is Option A from bf-20q9o (one function, fixes both paths, no key-format change). Commit it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] splitLinkID returns [nodeMAC, peerMAC] for the colon-joined LinkID the producer actually emits (verified by a quick unit assertion or debug print).
- [ ] With spaxel-sim streaming, gatherFusionLinks(pm) returns >=1 link (Fuse receives a non-empty links slice) — confirm via the FUSE-DBG log added in fusion.go showing links>=1.
- [ ] Both blob paths use the corrected split (3D gatherFusionLinks at main.go:5446 AND 2D localizer at main.go:2786).
- [ ] Change committed.

Landed splitLinkID fixed-width split (bf-561zr, commit b9f362c, pushed to origin main).

Root cause (bf-20q9o): CSIFrame.LinkID() joins the two MACs with ':' -> 'AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:11:22:33:44:55:66' (35 chars, boundary at index 17). splitLinkID scanned only for '-' and returned nil for every such link. Both fusion paths share splitLinkID (3D gatherFusionLinks main.go:5446 + 2D selfImprovingLocalizer main.go:2786), so gatherFusionLinks returned [] -> Fuse([]) -> 0 peaks -> 0 blobs.

Fix (Option A, one function, both paths, no key-format change): fixed-width split — len==35 -> split at index 17, handles both ':' (producer) and '-' (documented) separators. '-' scan kept as defensive fallback.

Acceptance:
- [x] splitLinkID returns [nodeMAC, peerMAC] for colon-joined producer LinkID — verified by TestSplitLinkID (6 table cases incl. upper/lower colon + dash) + TestSplitLinkIDProducerContract. Old code returned nil; new returns the two MACs.
- [x] gatherFusionLinks(pm) returns >=1 link for a colon-joined producer LinkID — verified by TestGatherFusionLinksProducerLinkID (function-level proof; the [FUSE-DBG] log in internal/fusion mirrors len(links) for runtime confirmation once a non-rejected node streams).
- [x] Both blob paths use the corrected split — single shared splitLinkID covers 2D (2786) + 3D (5446).
- [x] Committed + pushed.

issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-38dbu, 2026-08-02T12:40:41.183987047Z, author cli]
Found 2026-08-02 debugging why spaxel-build's docker-build step was failing consistently. Isolated the docker-build template into its own debug Workflow with podGC:OnWorkflowCompletion + live kubectl logs -f to catch it (podGC default -- OnPodCompletion -- deletes the pod before you can read anything, and the built-in retryStrategy exhausts fast enough that reactive polling for the retry pod consistently lost the race).

Actual kaniko error:
  Directory '/project/build' doesn't seem to be a CMake build directory. Refusing to automatically delete files in this directory. Delete the directory manually to 'clean' it.
  Adding "set-target"'s dependency "fullclean" to list of commands with default set of options.
  Executing action: fullclean
  error building image: error building stage: failed to execute command: waiting for process to exit: exit status 2

Root cause: the firmware-builder stage's two TARGETPLATFORM-conditional RUN commands (skip-and-placeholder for non-amd64, build-marker for amd64) are cached by kaniko on their LITERAL command text -- the shell 'if [ "$TARGETPLATFORM" != ... ]' logic is invisible to kaniko's cache key, so a cache entry produced by an arm64 build (which takes the placeholder branch, touching /project/build) can be served back to a later amd64 build, leaving /project/build in a state idf.py doesn't recognize as its own -- fullclean/set-target then refuses to proceed.

This is presumably a side effect of the recent multi-arch work (0c3ec2a 'wire multi-arch buildx support', 2a3acff 'remove hardcoded GOARCH=amd64 to enable arm64 builds') sharing kaniko's --cache-repo=ronaldraygun/cache across both architectures for the first time.

Immediate fix applied: moved the existing FIRMWARE_CACHE_BUST ARG (originally meant for sdkconfig.defaults changes) to before these two RUN commands instead of after -- it previously only busted layers from WORKDIR onward and never actually covered the poisoned ones. Bumped 2026-06-03 -> 2026-08-02. This unblocks the CI image build but does NOT fix the underlying kaniko/TARGETPLATFORM caching gap -- the same poisoning will recur the next time an arm64 and amd64 build interleave against the same cache repo.

Real fix (not attempted here, out of scope for an unrelated OTA/NTP deployment): make the conditional branches cache-safe per-platform, e.g. by putting TARGETPLATFORM into a file kaniko snapshots (so its value is part of the cache-relevant filesystem state) rather than relying on kaniko to key off the unevaluated shell condition, or split into genuinely separate COPY --from stages per architecture instead of runtime branching inside one RUN.

[migrated comment from bf-38dbu, 2026-08-02T13:12:13.405439335Z, author cli]
Correction (2026-08-02, same investigation): my first fix attempt (moving FIRMWARE_CACHE_BUST before the poisoned RUN commands) was insufficient and I verified this on real CI -- the layers were STILL served from cache ('Found cached layer, extracting to filesystem' for mkdir and both TARGETPLATFORM conditionals, confirmed via kaniko's own log output) even with the ARG declared earlier and bumped.

Root cause of why the first attempt didn't work: kaniko (like Docker's classic builder) only factors an ARG into a layer's cache key if that layer's OWN command text actually references/expands it. Being merely 'in scope' (declared by an earlier ARG instruction) isn't enough -- mkdir -p /project/build and the two conditionals never mention $FIRMWARE_CACHE_BUST anywhere in their command text, so its value changing had zero effect on their cache key.

Real fix: added 'echo "cache-bust: $FIRMWARE_CACHE_BUST" &&' as a prefix to all three RUN commands (mkdir + both conditionals), so the ARG's value is now part of each layer's literal command text and therefore part of kaniko's cache key.

Verified locally with a real (non-kaniko, but same ARG-substitution semantics) docker build --target firmware-builder: the build proceeded cleanly past idf.py set-target/fullclean into actual C compilation, where it previously failed at exactly that point. Also re-confirmed on iad-ci via an isolated podGC:OnWorkflowCompletion debug workflow with live log streaming (the only reliable way to catch kaniko's actual output before pod GC / retry churn destroys it).

[migrated labels from bf-38dbu]
deferred, umbrella
issue.title: Kaniko caches TARGETPLATFORM-conditional RUN steps across architectures, poisoning /project/build

issue.description: Split from bf-1018k. The capture artifacts under docs/notes/bf-4do5y-runtime-capture/ show that for the identity-less run, the .live.json file reports renderEvidence viz3d=false, meaning the 3D viz renderer never initializes during that capture. This is the strongest lead for why blobSeen=false persists now that the bf-11qvm SyntaxError fixes are in (pageErrors=0). Trace the init path in dashboard/js/viz3d.js and its consumers. Determine whether the no-identity mode skips or guards viz3d init, or whether init throws or cannot find its DOM target. Check module load order and whether init is gated on a message that never arrives in that mode. Correlate messageCount with what viz3d init expects. ACCEPTANCE: root cause of viz3d=false identified and documented in a comment on this bead (specific source line and why init does not happen). If a one-line fix is obvious, note it but do not apply yet (child 3 applies fixes).
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-2aogb, 2026-07-26T03:58:39.460196292Z, author cli]
[bf-2aogb diagnosis] ROOT CAUSE of renderEvidence viz3d=false

VERDICT: viz3d=false is NOT a renderer-init failure and is NOT identity-gated. The Three.js viz3d renderer initializes correctly in BOTH capture runs. The defect is that the module object is never exposed on `window`, so the capture harness (and every `if (window.Viz3D)` guard) cannot observe it.

SPECIFIC SOURCE LINE: dashboard/js/viz3d.js:9
    const Viz3D = (function () { ... })();
A top-level `const`/`let` lives in the GLOBAL LEXICAL ENVIRONMENT — it is NOT a property of the `window` (global object). Only `var` and explicit `window.x =` create window properties. So although the lexical `Viz3D` is fully functional and reachable by sibling scripts sharing that lexical scope, `window.Viz3D` stays undefined. HEAD's viz3d.js never assigns it (grep shows window.Viz3D only on the READ side of the layer-toggle wrappers at lines 4050/4060/4070/4080, never a write).

WHY INIT "DOES NOT HAPPEN" (observationally): It DOES happen. Console shows [Spaxel] Scene initialized; pageErrors=0; no throw; WebGL/swiftshader comes up ([FXAA] Desktop detected, skipping FXAA). Live blobs reach the in-memory map: app.js:1254 and 1296 call Viz3D.handleLocUpdate({blobs}) -> applyLocUpdate -> _blobs3D.set(b.id, obj) (viz3d.js:776-780). The console confirms blobs arriving: [Spaxel] Received snapshot, rebuilding state, then Event: detection ... by blob #3/#4.

The harness scripts/capture-dashboard-console.mjs probes window.Viz3D.getBlobStates() — lines 156-159 (blobSeen loop) and 181-186 (renderEvidence). Because window.Viz3D is undefined, both short-circuit -> {page:'live', viz3d:false} and blobSeen=false, EVEN THOUGH _blobs3D is populated with live blobs. So blobSeen=false is a pure artifact of the unreachable probe, not of missing blobs.

NOT IDENTITY-SPECIFIC: BOTH identity-less.live.json AND identity.live.json report viz3d=false and blobSeen=false. The init path is identical in both modes — there is no identity gate on viz3d init, no DOM-target lookup failure, and no message viz3d waits on that fails to arrive in identity-less mode. messageCount (110 vs 98) is irrelevant: the renderer does not gate init on a message count. The "no-identity mode skips viz3d" hypothesis is disproven.

ONE-LINE FIX (sufficient; NOT applied here — child 3 owns it). At the end of viz3d.js after the IIFE:
    if (typeof window !== 'undefined') { window.Viz3D = Viz3D; }
This alone fixes viz3d/blobSeen: getBlobStates() (viz3d.js:3491) reads the live _blobs3D map that handleLocUpdate populates, so once exposed the harness reports viz3d:true / blobCount>0 / blobSeen:true. NOTE: this exact fix is ALREADY present uncommitted in the working tree (viz3d.js +15 lines incl. comment, mtime 23:45); the capture artifacts (23:36) predate it, which is why they still show viz3d=false. Child 3 should commit it and re-run the capture to confirm viz3d->true.
Collateral no-op guards the same fix repairs: HTML layer toggles (toggleFlowLayer/Dwell/Corridor/setFlowTimeFilter), explainability.js X-ray overlay, anomaly.js zone rendering, quick-actions follow.
issue.title: Diagnose viz3d renderer non-init in identity-less dashboard capture

issue.description:
Part of ADR-003 / bf-4j97b.

Manager.OverrideRole (mothership/internal/fleet/manager.go:277-289) persists a role via registry.SetNodeRole, but there is no override/lock flag in the registry, and the fleet optimiser was observed re-asserting role=tx_rx on a ~60s cadence during bring-up ('Sent role=tx_rx to node ...' repeating in the mothership log).

Consequence: an operator setting role=passive for ambient sensing will have it silently reverted within a minute, which will look like passive mode 'not working'.

Fix: add a role-override/lock flag the optimiser respects, or have the optimiser treat manually-set roles as pinned.
issue.title: Preserve operator role override against fleet re-optimisation

issue.description:
Spaxel is a public repo (GitHub mirror) but the only running instance
(spaxel.ardenone.com) sits behind ardenone-com-traefik-auth, so nobody
outside the household can ever see the dashboard in action. Screenshots
in the README are the only way a prospective self-hoster sees the product
before installing hardware.

Add an SPAXEL_DEMO_MODE environment variable (default false) that, when
set:
- Rejects all mutating REST endpoints (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE on nodes,
  floor plans, automations, provisioning, calibration, etc.) with a clear
  403 + "demo mode" message.
- Serves the dashboard without requiring a PIN.
- Optionally caps dashboard WebSocket client count lower than the default
  SPAXEL_MAX_DASHBOARD_CLIENTS to bound a public instance's resource use.

This is a prerequisite for ever safely exposing a Spaxel instance (e.g.
fed by spaxel-sim, see the sibling simulator-activation bead) on a public,
unauthenticated route without risking a stranger reconfiguring someone's
floor plan or automations. Ship the flag and its enforcement in mothership
first; the actual public-routing decision (new subdomain, rate limiting,
etc.) is a separate follow-on once this exists.

Reference: mothership REST API (docs/plan/plan.md, REST API Specification
section) and its environment variable table (Deployment section).

issue.description:
Split-child of bf-3xkrb. READ-ONLY DIAGNOSIS — produce a written root-cause, NO code change.

GOAL: Determine exactly which path cmd/sim provisionToken() takes and why the mothership rejects the resulting token under SPAXEL_MIGRATION_WINDOW_HOURS=0, so the fix child has a CONFIRMED mechanism (parent only had a LIKELY MECHANISM).

INVESTIGATE (correct paths — parent said ingestion/server.go at repo root; that is WRONG):
- mothership/cmd/sim/main.go:724 provisionToken() — POSTs /api/provision {mac:...}, reads result[node_token] (line 750); on non-200 or missing field falls back to synthetic HMAC with LITERAL 'sim-install-secret' (line 760).
- mothership/internal/provisioning/server.go:153 HandleProvision — what does it return? field name? does it honor the strict window? which InstallSecret?
- mothership/internal/provisioning/server.go:135 ValidateToken(mac, token) — what secret/method does it expect?
- mothership/internal/ingestion/server.go:547,549 — the reject site; confirm it calls ValidateToken and which token it receives (hello.Token vs header).
- Reconcile e2e harness claim (mothership/tests/e2e/e2e_test.go:85-101) that sim 'defaults to --provision' should work — explain the contradiction.
- Note prior commit 285d9eb (feat(sim): provision real per-node HMAC token by default, bf-4mle6) — landed or regressed?

DELIVERABLE: A comment on bf-3xkrb naming ONE concrete root cause with file:line evidence (e.g. 'provisionToken() hits fallback because /api/provision returns field X not node_token' or 'real token obtained but ValidateToken uses a different secret'). State whether the fix belongs in cmd/sim/main.go, internal/provisioning/server.go, or both.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Written root-cause comment with a single specific file:line-backed mechanism (not 'likely').
- Explicit verdict on whether fix touches cmd/sim/main.go, internal/provisioning/server.go, or both.
- No production code changed.
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-3l0b0, 2026-07-26T16:43:57.106196818Z, author cli]
DONE (read-only diagnosis; no code changed). Root cause confirmed and posted as comment 227 on parent bf-3xkrb.

Single confirmed mechanism: mothership/cmd/sim/main.go provisionToken() (:724) mints ONE token for the hardcoded MAC AA:BB:CC:00:00:00 (:744) and connectNodes() reuses it for every node (:605-613, :642), but each node announces a different MAC (generateMAC(i)=AA:BB:CC:00:00:0{i}, :431-439/:663). ingestion validator recomputes HMAC over the announced MAC (ingestion/server.go:537 -> provisioning/server.go:135-143), so only node 0 validates; nodes 1..N mismatch. Under SPAXEL_MIGRATION_WINDOW_HOURS=0 the migrationDeadline is never set (config.go:4626) so the Unpaired-grace branch (ingestion/server.go:539-542) is skipped and they are hard-rejected at :549. The 24h default window masks it via the Unpaired branch.

Key correction to the parent's LIKELY mechanism: the synthetic fallback secret "sim-install-secret" (sim:760) is NOT the active path — the real per-MAC token IS fetched (field name node_token matches). Confirmed mechanism is the single-shared-token / per-node-MAC mismatch.

Reconciled the e2e harness contradiction: the comment (e2e_test.go:85-101) describes repo-root cmd/sim/ (resolveTokens, commit 285d9eb), but moduleRoot()=mothership/ so the harness builds mothership/cmd/sim/ (broken copy, no resolveTokens). Commit 285d9eb landed only in the unused-root copy.

Verdict: fix belongs in mothership/cmd/sim/main.go only (provision per-node token). No change to provisioning/server.go or ingestion/server.go.
issue.title: Root-cause why provisioned sim tokens are rejected under the strict window

issue.description:
Blocks bf-436bh. Cheap check that could change the whole partition design.

The build assumes 4MB (CONFIG_ESPTOOLPY_FLASHSIZE_4MB=y), and the 2026-07-28 flash backup is exactly 4 MiB — but that proves nothing, because flash-chunks.sh dumped it with an explicit --flash-size 4MB. sdkconfig.defaults itself hedges: 'Safe on 16MB boards: spi_flash only panics when physical < header, not when physical > header.'

If the modules are actually 16MB:
- A/B slots can be sized generously instead of squeezed
- the HTTPS + signed-app headroom tension (bf-1uefm, bf-436bh) largely disappears
- a factory recovery image becomes affordable alongside A/B

Run 'esptool flash-id' on a node and record the detected size. Do this BEFORE committing to a partitions.csv, since changing it later needs physical access to every node.
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-410ec, 2026-07-31T02:11:13.978299588Z, author cli]
ANSWERED ON HARDWARE 2026-07-30. The modules really are 4MB — the sdkconfig 'Safe on 16MB boards' hedge does not apply to this hardware.

  esptool --chip esp32s3 --port /dev/ttyACM0 flash-id
    MAC:                50:78:7d:1a:3d:c8
    Manufacturer: 20
    Device: 4016
    Detected flash size: 4MB

Device ID 0x4016 decodes as 2^22 = 4,194,304 bytes, consistent with the reported 4MB.

Consequences:
- the 4MB A/B layout proposed on bf-436bh stands as specified; no re-sizing for a larger part
- the headroom tension is REAL, not hypothetical: 1,623,392 B app in a 2,031,616 B slot leaves ~399 KiB, and HTTPS + signed-app verification (bf-1uefm) will consume a large share of it
- that makes the NimBLE evaluation (bf-5ryzr) materially more important — it is the main lever for reclaiming space on this hardware
- 4MB cannot hold A/B plus a factory recovery image, so dropping factory is confirmed as the necessary choice rather than merely the conventional one

Note esptool flash-id completed cleanly here, unlike the read-flash that wedged the device earlier (bf-4z6wh) — the lighter operation appears lower risk, though the failure mode is not yet understood.

[migrated labels from bf-410ec]
ota
issue.title: Confirm physical flash capacity (esptool flash-id) before finalising the A/B partition table

issue.description:
## Goal
Add a GET /api/doctor endpoint that diagnoses common misconfiguration before the user concludes the system is broken. Complements /healthz (runtime state) with pre-flight checks (configuration correctness).

## Endpoint

GET /api/doctor
- Requires session cookie (same as all /api/* endpoints)
- Returns 200 with a JSON report regardless of check results (HTTP status reflects reachability, not check results)

## Checks to run

| Check | Pass condition | Fail message |
|---|---|---|
| data_dir_writable | /data is writable and has >100 MB free | 'Data directory not writable' or 'Disk space low: Nf MB free' |
| db_integrity | PRAGMA integrity_check returns 'ok' | 'SQLite integrity check failed' |
| firmware_dir | /firmware contains at least one *.bin file | 'No firmware binaries found — OTA updates unavailable' |
| mdns_binding | mDNS service is registered (or SPAXEL_MDNS_ENABLED=false) | 'mDNS not advertising — nodes cannot auto-discover mothership' |
| mqtt_reachable | If SPAXEL_MQTT_BROKER is set: TCP connect to broker succeeds within 3s | 'MQTT broker unreachable: <broker_url>' |
| ntp_reachable | UDP ping to SPAXEL_NTP_SERVER:123 resolves within 3s | 'NTP server unreachable — node clock sync may fail' |
| install_secret | install_secret row exists in auth table | 'Installation secret missing — re-run container to regenerate' |
| pin_configured | pin_bcrypt is non-null in auth table | 'Dashboard PIN not configured — run first-time setup' |
| node_token_consistency | All nodes in registry have non-null node_token | 'N nodes missing auth tokens — re-provision via Web Serial' |

## Response format

{
  'checks': [
    {'name': 'db_integrity', 'status': 'ok', 'message': null},
    {'name': 'mqtt_reachable', 'status': 'warn', 'message': 'MQTT broker unreachable: mqtt://ha.local:1883'},
    {'name': 'firmware_dir', 'status': 'error', 'message': 'No firmware binaries found'}
  ],
  'overall': 'warn',   // 'ok' | 'warn' | 'error' (worst of all checks)
  'checked_at': '2024-03-15T07:00:00Z'
}

Status levels: 'ok' (pass), 'warn' (degraded but functional), 'error' (action required).

## Dashboard integration
- Command palette: 'doctor' → calls /api/doctor, shows results inline
- Guided troubleshooting (Component 36): 'Node offline' flow links to 'Run diagnostics' which calls /api/doctor
- /healthz already covers runtime health; /api/doctor covers configuration health — keep them separate

## Acceptance
- GET /api/doctor returns 200 with all checks when fully configured
- Reports 'firmware_dir: error' when /firmware is empty
- Reports 'mqtt_reachable: warn' when MQTT broker env is set but broker is unreachable
- Unit tests cover each check in isolation with mocked dependencies
issue.title: API: GET /api/doctor — pre-flight configuration diagnostic

issue.description:
Child 1 of the bf-bq9 sub-split (parent bf-bq9; grandparent bf-2i4; great-grandparent bf-56v; great-great-grandparent bf-4ne). Depends on sibling bf-3id (per-test failure recovery: g_test_jmp + g_failure_count + test_record_failure, already landed). This child is the entry-point core of the runner — the piece that makes a failing assertion non-fatal.

Scope (extend firmware/test/test_runner.c):
- Add a comment block above main() naming the documented run command: `make -C firmware/test test` (per the bf-1xs header contract and the bf-56v gcc-harness decision record). make compiles every test_*.c plus this runner with plain gcc and runs the binary; main()'s exit code is what make propagates.
- Implement int main(void): iterate the registry g_tests[] (the TEST() constructors have already fully populated it before main runs). For each test, setjmp(g_test_jmp) — the per-test target from sibling bf-3id — then call g_tests[i].fn(). On the direct setjmp return (0) the body ran clean: print "PASS: <name>" and bump a local passed counter. On a longjmp return (non-zero) a failed assertion tripped test_record_failure(): print "FAIL: <name>" and bump a local failed counter. Either way advance to the next test, so one test's failure never blocks the rest.
- For now return 0 — the non-zero-on-failure exit code is a later child.

Acceptance criteria:
- firmware/test/test_runner.c has an int main(void) that drives every registered test through the per-test setjmp/longjmp recovery loop, printing one PASS/FAIL line per test.
- A failing assertion in one test does NOT prevent later tests from running (the per-test setjmp/longjmp).
- A comment block above main() documents the run command `make -C firmware/test test`.
- Compiles cleanly with gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra; with at least one TEST() defined it links, runs, and exits 0 when all tests pass.
- No changes to firmware/main/* or firmware/CMakeLists.txt.

issue.description:
Part of ADR-003 / bf-4j97b. This is why a node with completely dead CSI looks healthy.

firmware/main/websocket.c health message:
  cJSON_AddNumberToObject(root, "csi_rate_hz", g_state.packet_rate);

g_state.packet_rate is the CONFIGURED target loaded from NVS (20 Hz), not a measurement. A node capturing and sending zero CSI frames reports csi_rate_hz=20 forever.

Meanwhile firmware/main/csi.c already maintains the real counter — s_stats.frames_sent, incremented only on a successful websocket_send_csi — and never reports it.

Consequence: the single metric an operator would use to answer 'is this node actually sensing?' is a restatement of its configuration. Observed live: node online, role=passive, /api/links empty, /api/diagnostics {} — and nothing in the health data indicated a problem.

Fix: report a measured rate computed from the s_stats.frames_sent delta over the health interval. Keep the configured target as a separate field if useful, but the field named csi_rate_hz must reflect reality.
issue.notes:
[migrated labels from bf-54cx2]
ambient-sensing
issue.title: Node reports configured csi_rate_hz, not measured — a node emitting zero CSI still reports 20 Hz

issue.description:
Part of ADR-003 / bf-4j97b.

Nodes are intended to be distributed where they have power and left there, so the firmware fixes in this epic (CSI arming, and ADR-002 provisioning transport) must be deliverable without physical recovery.

The infrastructure exists but has never been exercised on real hardware:
- firmware/partitions.csv: factory (1.9MB) + ota_0 (1.9MB) + otadata, A/B with rollback
- CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_APP_ROLLBACK_ENABLE=y, CONFIG_APP_ROLLBACK_ENABLE=y
- endpoints: /api/nodes/{mac}/ota, /api/nodes/update-all, /api/firmware/upload, /api/firmware/ota-all, /api/firmware/progress
- firmware/main/websocket.c confirms OTA partition valid on first role message after boot (esp_ota_mark_app_valid_cancel_rollback)

Validate: upload a firmware image, OTA a real node, confirm it boots the new slot, confirm rollback fires on a deliberately-bad image. Note the rollback-confirm path depends on receiving a role message within 60s of connecting (websocket.c:41) — verify that interacts correctly with the CSI-arming change in bf-3mb8j.
issue.notes:
OTA validation documented. Update delivery is proven reliable (3/3 cycles, A/B alternation confirmed from 2026-08-06/07). Rollback mechanism exists but NEVER tested on hardware.

KEY FINDINGS:
- A/B partitions (ota_0/ota_1) with rollback enabled: CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_APP_ROLLBACK_ENABLE=y, CONFIG_APP_ROLLBACK_ENABLE=y
- Dual-requirement validation: role message + CSI flowing (prevents bad image lock-in)
- 60-second timeout triggers forced reboot if validation fails
- CSI-arming fix (bf-3mb8j) ensures CSI enables even when role unchanged

MISSING VALIDATION (blocked by no test hardware):
1. Deliberately-bad image rollback never tested
2. CSI-arming requirement enforcement never verified
3. 60-second timeout behavior never observed

DOCUMENTATION CREATED:
- firmware/test/OTA_ROLLBACK_VALIDATION_PROCEDURE.md (complete test procedure)
- Requires: ESP32-S3 + AP + mothership + ESP-IDF environment

VALIDATION PROCEDURE:
1. Build good firmware (baseline)
2. Build bad firmware (CSI broken but boots)
3. Test good image OTA (should validate)
4. Test bad image OTA (should timeout after 60s and rollback)
5. Verify CSI-arming enforcement (both role + CSI required)

Next action: When test hardware is available, execute documented procedure and record results.
issue.title: Validate OTA end to end before distributing nodes to powered locations

issue.description:
Parent: bf-11qvm (split). Fix the two STRUCTURAL SyntaxErrors of the same type:

1. dashboard/js/ambient.js ~line 715 — SyntaxError: Unexpected token ')'. Context: the file ends an IIFE with 'console.log(...); })();'. An 'Unexpected token )' at the IIFE terminator means a brace/paren is unbalanced INSIDE the IIFE body, so the closing ')();' does not line up with its opener. Find the mismatched brace/paren earlier in the file.

2. dashboard/js/viz3d.js ~line 3635 — SyntaxError: Unexpected token ')'. Context: a '});' closing a callback. Same class of bug: an unbalanced brace/paren earlier in that callback or its enclosing function makes the closing '})' unexpected.

Both are brace/paren-balance bugs, NOT localized typos. APPROACH: brace/paren-match each file (bisect with node --check, or check the opener that lines up with the reported closing token). Do NOT blindly add/remove tokens — confirm intended nesting so runtime behavior is unchanged.

SCOPE: dashboard/js/ambient.js and dashboard/js/viz3d.js ONLY.

ACCEPTANCE:
- [ ] node --check dashboard/js/ambient.js passes (0 SyntaxError).
- [ ] node --check dashboard/js/viz3d.js passes (0 SyntaxError).
- [ ] IIFE/callback structure intact; no behavior change — only brace/paren balance corrected.
issue.notes:

- ambient.js: missing closing brace for handleWebSocketMessage() was added
- viz3d.js: missing closing brace for if(!originalState) block in highlightLinks was added

issue.close_reason: Fixed and verified on hardware — esp_sntp_stop() before reconfiguring, matching the existing periodic-resync pattern
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-1y316, 2026-08-02T01:50:23.468672673Z, author cli]
Found and fixed (2026-08-01, same session as bf-5x46/3c282/5vwo8/23nar and the new embedded NTP server feature).

ntp_start_sync() (firmware/main/ntp.c) called esp_sntp_setoperatingmode() + esp_sntp_init() unconditionally, with no check for whether the SNTP client was already running. ESP-IDF treats that as a hard assertion failure, not a soft error:

  assert failed: sntp_setoperatingmode /IDF/components/lwip/lwip/src/apps/sntp/sntp.c:730 (Operating mode must not be set while SNTP client is running)

-- which aborts and reboots the whole node.

ntp_start_sync() is called more than once per boot in two real, ordinary scenarios, not just once at startup:
  1. main.c calls it on the initial WiFi connect AND again on NODE_STATE_WIFI_LOST recovery -- i.e. ANY WiFi hiccup that reconnects without a full node reboot (AP restart, brief interference) crashes the node once NTP already synced once this boot.
  2. handle_config_msg (websocket.c) calls it whenever the mothership pushes a new ntp_server value at runtime.

Reproduced via (2): testing the new embedded SNTP server feature, pushing a live NTP config change to an already-connected, already-synced node crashed it immediately with the assertion above. This is a real, previously-undiscovered bug -- (2)'s code path existed already but was unreachable before this session (SendNTPServerToMAC, the function that triggers it, had no callers -- see bf-5bunq), so nothing had ever exercised it. (1) is more concerning: it's a plain WiFi reconnect, something that will happen routinely on any real deployment, and as far as I can tell nothing in earlier testing this session happened to trigger NODE_STATE_WIFI_LOST specifically (my mothership-restart repro tests kept WiFi associated throughout, only disrupting the WS/mothership layer) -- so this may have been silently crashing nodes in the field already without anyone connecting the dots to NTP.

Fix: esp_sntp_stop() before reconfiguring, mirroring the pattern the file's own periodic_resync_callback() already used correctly (stop, then reconfigure, then re-init) -- ntp_start_sync() just didn't follow its own file's established pattern.

Verified on hardware: pushed a live NTP config change to an already-synced node -- 'NTP server changed to: 192.168.50.1' -> 'Starting NTP sync with server: 192.168.50.1' -> 'NTP synchronized: ...' in ~370ms, no crash, no reboot. Confirmed the pre-fix build crashed on the identical action (same repro, same debug endpoint, prior binary).
issue.title: ntp_start_sync() crashes the node on any re-call — WiFi reconnect or NTP config push both trigger it

issue.description:
Parent: bf-1cgqe. Add a regression test so the 404/text/plain failure (diagnosed in the bf-1cgqe comment) cannot silently recur. Depends on the fallback-fix child.

SCOPE:
- Add a Go test under mothership/cmd/mothership/ (or appropriate _test.go) that exercises the dashboard static handler against the real dashboard/ assets and asserts, via GET:
    GET /css/tokens.css -> 200, Content-Type text/css
    GET /js/app.js      -> 200, Content-Type text/javascript (or application/javascript)

issue.description:
Pre-existing test failure at main (verified 2026-08-20 against a clean git-archive of HEAD, independent of any working-tree edits):

--- FAIL: TestNetworkSettingsHandler_PutAllowsEmptyPasswordForOpenNetwork
    network_settings_test.go:168: expected configured=false when password is empty, got true

mothership/internal/api/network_settings.go response() computes Configured as (ssid != "" && hasPass) where hasPass only checks that the settings key EXISTS — so storing an empty password (open network) yields configured=true. The test (network_settings_test.go:143-169) encodes the opposite contract with a deliberate comment: SSID alone is not enough for the provisioning defaulting logic (ADR-005) to treat fleet WiFi as complete.

Fix direction: either Configured should require a non-empty password, or the provisioning-side consumer should be reconciled with the open-network case — decide which contract is authoritative and align handler+test. Discovered while gating bead spaxel-d0e38d23 (firmware transport abstraction, ADR-002 part 2) — that bead touches firmware only and does not affect this test.
issue.notes:
**ADR-005 Analysis (CORRECTED 2026-08-29):**

After locating and reading ADR-005 directly (line 4440 in plan.md), the contract is UNAMBIGUOUS:

**ADR-005 Decision Point 3 states:**
> 'Warn clearly when neither source has credentials. No stored setting and no request-body override produces an empty WiFi section with a warning, **allowing open-network and captive-portal flows** while making the missing fleet configuration visible in the dashboard.'

**Critical distinction:** 'Allowing' open-network flows ≠ treating them as 'configured'. ADR-005 authorizes provisioning with empty credentials (for captive portal/onboarding), but does NOT require Configured=true for that case.

**Authoritative Contract from Implementation:**
From `network_settings.go` lines 142-148:
> 'Configured when SSID is set and a non-empty password exists. Empty password is valid for open networks but does NOT count as "configured" because SSID alone isn't enough for the provisioning defaulting logic.'

Code: `Configured: ssidStr != "" && hasPass && passStr != ""`

**Test Contract is CORRECT:**
The test at network_settings_test.go:164-169 correctly expects configured=false for empty password. Multiple test files (wifi_credential_edge_cases_test.go) confirm this.

**Resolution:**
- Current implementation (requiring non-empty password for Configured=true) is CORRECT per ADR-005
- The bead's 2026-08-24 notes misread ADR-005 by conflating 'allowing' with 'configured'
- Keep logic as-is: configured=false for open networks is the intended behavior
issue.title: NetworkSettingsHandler reports configured=true for open network with empty password (ADR-005)

Document the working procedure for building and flashing `firmware/` to a real ESP32-S3, including a flashing-reliability workaround discovered during the 2026-07-28 bring-up. Without this, the next person to attempt a hardware flash will lose hours rediscovering it — the failure mode is loud but extremely misleading.

**Build (works, no repo changes needed):** ESP-IDF v5.2 in Docker, `idf.py set-target esp32s3 build`. Produces a 1,631,552-byte app that fits the 0x1F0000 factory partition with ~20% free. Note that if the Docker daemon uses userns-remap, running the container as the host uid fails with a permission error on the bind mount — run as the container default instead, which maps to the host user.

**Flashing problem:** with `esptool` 5.2.0 against this board's native USB-Serial/JTAG interface, large `write-flash` operations are unreliable. The stub flasher dies partway and esptool reports a *chip-side* panic, e.g.:

    A fatal error occurred: Guru Meditation Error detected (StoreProhibited)
    A fatal error occurred: Guru Meditation Error detected (IllegalInstruction)
    A fatal error occurred: The chip stopped responding

The exception type varies run to run. **These messages are misleading — they are artifacts of the flashing transport, not a firmware crash.** During bring-up they were initially read as evidence that the firmware panicked on boot; it does not. Once the image is fully written the firmware boots cleanly every time. Anyone debugging a "crashing" ESP32 here should confirm a complete, verified flash before believing a panic.

Related observations:
- Writes of roughly 20 KB and under succeed reliably; 64 KB and 256 KB writes fail consistently. The boundary is not a clean cutoff — a 32 KB write succeeded where a 24 KB write failed, so treat it as flaky-above-a-threshold rather than a fixed limit.
- `erase-flash` and `erase-region` fail the same way. Full-chip erase could not be completed at all.
- `--before usb-reset` is required to reliably enter download mode on this interface; `--before default-reset` is unreliable once a non-booting image is present.
- With `--after no-reset`, esptool 5.2.0 fails during teardown in `soft_reset()` even when the write itself verified — read the "Hash of data verified" line, not the exit status.
- The reliable workaround: split the app image into 32 KB chunks and write each in its own invocation with retries. 50 chunks, all verified. A working script was left on the bench host at `~/spaxel-fw/flash-chunks.sh` and should be folded into this repo (e.g. `scripts/flash-esp32s3.sh`) rather than left on one machine.

**Monitoring:** the console must be routed to USB-Serial/JTAG or the board is silent (see the console-routing sibling bead). A plain `cat /dev/ttyACM0` opened after reset only catches a fragment; open the port, assert reset via the control lines, then read continuously from the same handle.

Scope:
- Add a firmware build/flash/monitor runbook under `docs/notes/`.
- Commit a chunked-flash helper script into `scripts/` with the retry loop.
- Record the original board flash backup location and the advice to back up before first flash.

Acceptance criteria:
- A runbook exists that takes someone from clean checkout to a booting node with observable logs, without rediscovering any of the above.
- The chunked-flash script is committed and has been used successfully end-to-end at least once.

[migrated comment from bf-26pa, 2026-08-01T02:21:00.060008695Z, author cli]
RUNBOOK GAP FOUND THE HARD WAY 2026-07-31 — flashing a native-USB-only ESP32-S3 requires a PHYSICAL POWER CYCLE afterwards, and esptool cannot substitute for it.

Sequence that cost about an hour:
1. Board put into download mode by holding BOOT while plugging in.
2. Flash succeeded — all four regions written and verified (digests matched).
3. Every attempt to boot the new firmware produced only the ROM banner
   (ESP-ROM:esp32s3-20210327, 26 bytes) and then silence. No association, no
   mothership connection. It looked exactly like a firmware that would not boot.

The firmware was fine. The chip never left download mode.

Diagnostic tells, all consistent:
- 'esptool --before no-reset' kept succeeding. That ONLY works if the chip is
  already in download mode.
- USB stayed Device 011 across every reset. A booting app re-enumerates; no
  re-enumeration means the app never took the USB peripheral.
- esptool prints 'Hard resetting via RTS pin...' and it is a NO-OP on this
  hardware: a native-USB-only board has no USB-UART bridge wiring DTR/RTS to
  EN/BOOT. The message is reassuring and means nothing here.

RUNBOOK STEPS TO DOCUMENT:
- After any flash entered via BOOT-hold, physically unplug/replug WITHOUT
  holding BOOT. That is the only way out of download mode on this board.
- Do not trust 'Hard resetting via RTS pin...' as evidence a reset occurred.
- To distinguish 'not booting' from 'booting but silent', check AP association
  and mothership connection — both are independent of the console.
- Related: opening /dev/ttyACM0 without 'stty -hupcl' RESETS the node, and a
  capture opened across a reset dies when the USB peripheral re-enumerates.
  Open the port AFTER the device has settled.

[migrated comment from bf-26pa, 2026-08-01T18:05:47.044466529Z, author cli]
Update (2026-08-01): plain stub-mode 'esptool write-flash' (no --no-stub, no chunking) wrote the full 1,623,824-byte app image to 0x20000 in one shot -- 18s wall clock, hash verified, no wedge. Also wrote bootloader.bin (0x0), partition-table.bin (0x8000), and ota_data_initial.bin (0x10000) individually via plain stub mode, all clean.

This contradicts the 2026-07-28 finding that large writes fail consistently via this interface -- but that testing was specifically with --no-stub. New data (also logged on bf-4z6wh) suggests --no-stub --before usb-reset write-flash is itself what wedges this board, independent of write size, and isn't needed at all: plain esptool write-flash (stub mode, default flags) handled everything including the full app in a single pass.

Revised recommendation: default to plain 'esptool --chip esp32s3 --port <port> write-flash ...' (stub mode, no special flags) for everything on this board. Only reach for the --no-stub chunked workaround (scripts/flash-esp32s3.sh, now committed) if plain stub-mode write-flash itself fails -- don't reach for it by default, since invoking --no-stub write-flash appears to be what caused the repeated wedges requiring physical replugs during the 2026-08-01 session.

issue.close_reason: Console configuration fix applied. The ESP32-S3 console default was already correctly set to USB-Serial/JTAG via CMakeLists.txt layering sdkconfig.usbjtag, with comprehensive documentation in README.md and a UART0 override path. The only defect was a missing CONFIG_ESP_CONSOLE_UART_NUM=-1 line in sdkconfig.usbjtag, which caused ESP-IDF to default to an incorrect UART number (4) instead of 'no UART' for the USB-Serial/JTAG profile. This has been corrected. A clean build now generates a valid USB-Serial/JTAG console configuration that passes verification and produces full boot logs on native-USB-only boards without manual sdkconfig edits. See commit c9b5d7c.
issue.description:
**A stock ESP32-S3 devkit connected by its native USB port is completely silent — no boot log, no panic output, no diagnostics.** This is the reason the three functional defects in this umbrella went undetected for so long: there was no way to see what the firmware was doing.

`firmware/sdkconfig.defaults` sets no `CONFIG_ESP_CONSOLE_*` option at all, so the build inherits the ESP-IDF default of UART0 as the primary console (generated config: `CONFIG_ESP_CONSOLE_UART_DEFAULT=y`, `CONFIG_ESP_CONSOLE_UART_NUM=0`). UART0 is GPIO43/44, which is unconnected on a board whose only host link is the chip's native USB-Serial/JTAG peripheral.

Measured on hardware with the stock (UART-console) build, across a 150 s capture on the host CDC device: only bootloader-stage output arrived (fragments up to `I (101) boot: End of partition table`, ~49 bytes total) and **no application-stage log line ever appeared** — despite the generated config also carrying `CONFIG_ESP_CONSOLE_SECONDARY_USB_SERIAL_JTAG=y`. Rebuilding with USB-Serial/JTAG as the *primary* console:

    CONFIG_ESP_CONSOLE_UART_DEFAULT=n
    CONFIG_ESP_CONSOLE_USB_SERIAL_JTAG=y

immediately produced the complete boot log through `app_main`, the provisioning window, WiFi init, mDNS, BLE and captive-portal startup — which is how every other defect in this umbrella was found. The secondary-console setting alone was not sufficient in practice; do not rely on it.

Scope:
- Decide and document the default console target for the ESP32-S3 build. Recommended: USB-Serial/JTAG primary, since the native port is what modern S3 devkits and bare modules expose and what a user is most likely to have plugged in.
- Make it selectable rather than hardcoded so bridge-equipped boards can keep UART0 — e.g. a board-variant defaults file (`sdkconfig.defaults.esp32s3` or an explicit `sdkconfig.usbjtag` layered via `SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS`) rather than editing the shared defaults in place.
- Document the choice and the override in the firmware build instructions so the next person to plug in a board is not debugging silence.

Acceptance criteria:
- A clean build flashed to a USB-Serial/JTAG-only ESP32-S3 prints the full boot log, including all `app_main`-stage lines, on the native USB CDC device with no manual sdkconfig edits.
- The UART0-console configuration remains reachable via a documented, tested override.
- Panic output (backtrace) is confirmed visible on the chosen console — deliberately trigger a fault once to verify, since diagnosing future field crashes depends on it.
issue.notes: Re-audited the existing implementation in 156eca9 (already an ancestor of HEAD): shared sdkconfig.defaults is board-neutral; CMake selects sdkconfig.usbjtag by default; sdkconfig.uart-console is the documented SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS override; generated-config verifier, panic-print settings, and host contract tests are present. Verification: make -C firmware/test test passed all tests; bash -n firmware/scripts/verify-console-config.sh and git diff --check passed. This checkout has no generated firmware/sdkconfig, ESP-IDF/idf.py/esptool/serial-monitor tools, or /dev/ttyACM*/ttyUSB* device, so a clean IDF build/flash and the acceptance-required deliberate hardware panic/backtrace capture cannot be performed here. No firmware files changed, so no commit or push was made. Leave bead open for bench verification.
issue.title: Console defaults to unconnected UART0 — USB-Serial/JTAG boards boot silently, hiding all diagnostics

Prerequisites: bf-4eal (deployment to 0.1.354) is complete.

Steps:
1. Open Chrome or Edge (Web Serial requires Chromium-based browser)
2. Navigate to spaxel.ardenone.com (auth required — use existing credentials)
3. Go to the provision / onboard page
4. Connect the ESP32-S3 dev board via USB-C
5. Click Flash/Provision — esptool.js will download firmware from mothership
   and write it to the device
6. Monitor the serial output: should boot, NOT crash with flash size mismatch
7. Expected: captive portal or WiFi connection attempt (node is unprovisioned)

If the device still shows the 16MB crash, check /api/firmware/manifest returns
a firmware binary whose image header byte[3] bits 4-7 = 0x4 (4MB), not 0x6 (16MB).

This is the validation step that confirms the 4MB fix works end-to-end.

issue.description:

Scope: create firmware/test/Makefile such that ONE command both compiles and runs the whole suite and propagates the binary's exit code:
- A 'test' goal = 'build run'. 'build' compiles every firmware/test/test_*.c (glob) PLUS test_runner.c with gcc (-std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -O2 -g) into a binary (e.g. build/spaxel_host_tests). 'run' executes it.

- make must propagate the test binary's non-zero exit (the default 'run' recipe does this; do not swallow it with a leading @ that ignores $?).
- Header comment names the single documented command 'make -C firmware/test test' (run from repo root) — this must match the command named in test_runner.h's header comment (child 1).

Acceptance criteria:
- firmware/test/Makefile exists.
- 'make -C firmware/test test' (the documented single command) compiles AND runs the suite.
- make propagates the binary's non-zero exit code (verified in child 4 by a failing assertion).
- A new firmware/test/test_*.c is compiled/linked with zero Makefile edits (wildcard + self-registering constructor).
- test_runner.c included exactly once (no duplicate main/registry symbol link errors).

- No changes to firmware/main/* or firmware/CMakeLists.txt.

## Goal

All dashboard pages (`index.html`, `ambient.html`, `fleet.html`, `simple.html`, `integrations.html`) share one design system per plan.md §8e.

## Scope

Create `dashboard/css/tokens.css` with CSS custom properties for:

- **Colors:** Radix `slate` scale (12 steps) as `--slate-1` … `--slate-12`. Accent: Radix `blue` scale. Semantic: `--ok` (green-9), `--warn` (amber-9), `--alert` (red-9).
- **Typography:** `--font-body`, `--font-mono`. Sizes: `--text-xs` (12), `--text-sm` (14), `--text-base` (16), `--text-lg` (20), `--text-2xl` (28).
- **Spacing:** `--space-1` (4px) through `--space-16` (64px) on the canonical scale.
- **Radius:** `--radius-control` (6px), `--radius-card` (10px), `--radius-modal` (16px).

Then refactor each existing CSS file to use these tokens instead of hard-coded values. Delete any light-theme rules; dashboard is dark-only.

`integrations.html` is the reference — its current look already approximates the target. Use it as the acceptance bar for other pages.

## Verification

- `grep -r "#[0-9a-fA-F]\{3,6\}" dashboard/css/` returns only uses inside `tokens.css`.
- Playwright screenshots of all five pages show one consistent theme.
- axe-core reports zero WCAG AA contrast violations.

Traceability: plan.md §8e.
issue.title: Adopt single design system (Radix dark tokens) across dashboard

issue.description:
Split-child 3 of 3 (final child) for parent bf-53ut. Builds on children 1 and 2 (setjmp guard + observable failure line). This child is the acceptance PROOF for the parent bead: demonstrate, by running the real harness, that a failing assertion in one test does not prevent later tests from running and does not abort the process.

Scope:
- Temporarily add an intentionally-failing TEST() (one that calls an ASSERT_* macro that fails, e.g. ASSERT_EQ(1, 2)) immediately followed by a passing TEST(), in a scratch file under firmware/test/ (or inline in an existing scratch test). This probe is verification-only and MUST NOT be committed.
- Run: make -C firmware/test test
- Confirm all three: (a) BOTH tests' per-test observable lines print — the failing test's line AND the passing test's line, in order; (b) the process COMPLETES (returns control to the loop / exits) rather than aborting or crashing; (c) tests after the failing one are not skipped.
- Remove the temporary failing/passing probe so the tree is left clean. When closing, capture the observed output (the two lines + confirmation the process completed) as a comment on this bead.

Acceptance criteria:
- With an intentionally-failing test placed before a passing test, make -C firmware/test test prints both tests' per-test lines and completes (exits) rather than aborting.
- The temporary verification probe is removed; the working tree is left clean (no stray test files committed).
- The end-to-end result is captured as a comment on this bead (the two observed lines + confirmation that the process completed).
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-vmik, 2026-07-03T22:59:56.030805309Z, author cli]
bf-vmik (child 3/3 of bf-53ut): END-TO-END ACCEPTANCE PROOF that a failing assertion does NOT block later tests and does NOT abort the process.

Method: temporarily added test_scratch_probe.c with two adjacent TEST()s (zz_ prefix so they sort last) — zz_probe_failing (ASSERT_EQ(1,2)) immediately before zz_probe_passing (ASSERT_EQ(2+2,4)) — ran make -C firmware/test test, then removed the probe.

IMPORTANT: had to run make clean first. A stale gitignored build/spaxel_host_tests binary from a prior interrupted attempt was newer than every source file, so make was re-running a probe baked into the OLD binary rather than rebuilding. A clean rebuild was required for a trustworthy result.

Observed stdout (in order):
  VMIK-PROBE: entered FAILING test body (about to assert 1==2)
  RUN: zz_probe_failing (assertion failed)
  VMIK-PROBE: entered PASSING test body (later test, runs anyway)
  RUN: zz_probe_passing
  30 passed, 1 failed of 31
Observed stderr (the failing test diagnostic):
  test_scratch_probe.c:25: ASSERT_EQ(1, 2) failed: got 1, want 2

All three criteria confirmed:
(a) BOTH per-test observable lines printed, in order — failing line immediately followed by passing line (adjacent on stdout).
(b) The process COMPLETED, not crashed. Running the binary directly (bypassing make) returned exit code 1, the documented clean failure-exit (non-zero because a test failed). It was NOT 134 (SIGABRT) or 139 (SIGSEGV): the setjmp/longjmp guard caught the failed assertion and main() returned normally — no abort.
(c) The test after the failing one was NOT skipped: its body printf genuinely printed (entered PASSING test body), and the UNREACHABLE line after the failing ASSERT_EQ did NOT print (longjmp aborted only the failing body). 30 of 31 tests passed; exactly 1 failed.

Probe removed; working tree left clean — firmware/test git status empty; baseline rebuilt to 29 passed, 0 failed of 29, exit 0. No code changes in this bead (children 1 and 2 — setjmp guard + observable failure line — were already committed); this bead is the acceptance proof.
issue.title: Verify end-to-end that a failing assertion does not block later tests

Part of ADR-003 / bf-4j97b.

Today a passive role with no BSSID is accepted, transmitted to the node, and results in a filter on 00:00:00:00:00:00 that matches nothing — the node looks healthy, reports health, and produces zero CSI. That silent-drop behaviour is the most expensive property of this bug class and cost a full bring-up session to diagnose.

Fix: reject role=passive with no BSSID at the API boundary (HTTP 400) and log-and-refuse at the sender in SendRoleToMAC. Fail loud.

issue.description:
Part of split of bf-brz. Depends on the CSI frame test child. This is the LAST child; closing it unblocks the parent umbrella.

Goal: add a host-based unit test for the serial provisioning JSON parse/validate logic in firmware/main/provision.c.

Context: provision_listen_window() reads lines from UART and uses cJSON. The testable pure logic is the per-line decision: valid {"provision":{...}} -> success (writes NVS, would respond {"ok":true,"mac":...}); invalid JSON -> {"ok":false,"error":"invalid_json"}; valid JSON missing the provision key -> {"ok":false,"error":"missing_provision_key"}; NVS write failure -> {"ok":false,"error":"nvs_write_failed"}. cJSON itself is pure C and host-compilable.

Approach:
- Extract the line-parse decision into a pure host-compilable function (e.g. provision_parse_line(const char *line) -> result enum / error string), factored out of provision_listen_window. NVS writes can be stubbed for the host test. Keep production provision.c behavior identical.
- Add at least one valid provisioning JSON case and at least one invalid JSON case (and ideally the missing-provision-key case).

Acceptance criteria:
- A test under firmware/test/ covers at least one valid + one invalid provisioning JSON case, asserting the ok:true / ok:false (invalid_json) decision.
- The full firmware/test/ suite runs green under the single documented command and exits non-zero on failure.
- firmware/main/ production behavior is unchanged (extraction is refactor-only) and the firmware build still succeeds.
issue.title: Add serial provisioning JSON parser host test

issue.description:
Part of ADR-004 / bf-1447x (surfaced during OTA testing).

Node boot log:
  I (28262) wifi: Querying mDNS for spaxel._spaxel.local:8080
  W (33352) wifi: mDNS query failed or no results
  I (33352) spaxel: Using cached mothership IP: 192.168.50.1

The mothership was running with SPAXEL_MDNS_ENABLED=true and logs 'mDNS advertising spaxel._spaxel._tcp.local:8080'. The node's query still found nothing and fell back to its provisioned ms_ip.

Harmless in this test only because a static ms_ip had been provisioned via the captive portal. For zero-config onboarding — the documented design — mDNS is the discovery path and it is not working.

Investigate: which interface the mothership advertises on (it was bound to 192.168.50.1 on the AP interface), whether the query reaches it, and whether the k8s deployment's SPAXEL_MDNS_ENABLED=false has masked this everywhere else.
issue.title: mDNS discovery fails on the node — 'mDNS query failed or no results' despite SPAXEL_MDNS_ENABLED=true

## Goal
Dedicated display mode for wall-mounted tablets or always-on screens. Served at /ambient as separate lightweight route.

## Scope
- Simplified, stylized top-down floor plan — clean lines, soft rounded corners, no UI chrome
- People appear as softly glowing colored circles (BLE-identified) or neutral dots (unknown), with names
- Room labels show subtle occupancy: 'Kitchen · Alice' or 'Bedroom · Empty'
- Smooth, calm animations: dots drift with interpolated positions, no jitter, no snapping
- No toolbar, no buttons, no panels — just floor plan, people, small status line
- Time-of-day awareness: morning (bright/cool), day (neutral), evening (warm/amber), night (very dim, minimal)
- Adaptive behavior: house empty 30+ min → screen goes fully dark, 'All secure' in tiny text
- Alert event: entire display transitions to alert mode with pulsing red border, large text, action buttons
- Morning briefing integration: when first person detected, display briefly shows briefing text before fading to ambient

## Implementation
/ambient route serving lightweight HTML page
No Three.js — use Canvas 2D or SVG for minimal resource usage
WebSocket receives same dashboard feed but only uses blob positions, zone counts, alerts
<30 MB RAM, <5% CPU on 2018 iPad

## Acceptance
- Ambient mode runs unattended on wall-mounted tablet for 7+ days
- Time-of-day palette transitions smoothly
- Alert mode breaks the calm appropriately
- Morning briefing displays on first detection
- Resource usage: <30 MB RAM, <5% CPU

issue.notes:
Fix verified - already implemented in commit 72e7e1c (2026-08-20).

The reconnect flap issue has been resolved with a 200ms debounce window after WebSocket connect:

**Implementation (websocket.c:342-359):**
- Tracks connection timestamp in s_last_connect_time_us
- Ignores disconnect events within 200ms of successful connection
- Prevents spurious disconnects during connection stabilization

**Root cause addressed:**
During WebSocket reconnection teardown and setup, spurious disconnect events were firing before the new connection stabilized, triggering state machine transitions back into reconnection.

**Fix effectiveness:**
The 200ms debounce window eliminates the 1-2 transient disconnect flap pattern while preserving real disconnect detection for genuine connection losses.

Code reference lines 342-359 in websocket.c with explicit comment referencing this bead (spaxel-61de1fce) and ADR-004.
issue.title: Residual reconnect flap: 1-2 transient disconnects before a mothership-restart reconnect settles

issue.description:
Third link of the bf-34lwt split. Confirm that the migration window — not tokens — is what accepts tokenless sim nodes, and pin down exactly when REJECT fires. This proves current 'no reject' is a 24h-window MASK, not a real fix.

## Scope (cite file:line)
5. The only thing accepting sim nodes is the migration window: `internal/ingestion/server.go`. MigrationWindowHours DEFAULTS TO 24 (`internal/config/config.go`), so a fresh boot opens a 24h window → sim nodes accepted as Unpaired, no reject (matches PROGRESS.md bf-3hji).
6. Therefore REJECT fires ONLY when the window is closed: `SPAXEL_MIGRATION_WINDOW_HOURS=0` (deadline never set → IsZero() → reject branch), OR uptime > 24h. In those cases every sim node logs 'missing token' → `sendReject(conn, 'invalid_token')` → disconnect.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Quoted file:line(s) showing MigrationWindowHours default = 24 and the migration-deadline acceptance branch.
- [ ] Quoted file:line of the reject branch (window closed / IsZero()) and the `sendReject(...,'invalid_token')` call.
- [ ] Explicit statement: current 'no reject' is a 24h-window MASK, not a real fix — REJECT returns when window=0 or uptime>24h.
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-2hdbg, 2026-07-07T11:24:59.961980678Z, author cli]
DONE — committed docs(bf-2hdbg) 8116dc8, pushed to origin main (PROGRESS.md only; unrelated e2e_test.go/.beads bookkeeping left uncommitted).

Confirmed against current source that the migration window — not tokens — is the sole acceptor of tokenless sim nodes:

- config.go:139 MigrationWindowHours defaults to 24 (config.go:43 '0 = disabled'); main.go:4495-4497 installs deadline=now+24h only when >0, so a fresh boot opens the window.
- server.go:510-518 acceptance branch gates purely on server.go:515 (!deadline.IsZero() && time.Now().Before(deadline)); tokenOK (server.go:513) is irrelevant — tokenless node admitted as Unpaired.
- server.go:519-526 reject branch (else of 515) → server.go:525 sendReject(conn,"invalid_token") + conn.Close(); sendReject emits {"type":"reject","reason":"invalid_token"} (server.go:841-845).

Conclusion: current 'no reject' is a 24h-window MASK, not a real fix. REJECT returns when SPAXEL_MIGRATION_WINDOW_HOURS=0 (deadline never set → IsZero() → reject) OR uptime > 24h (Before(deadline) false → reject). Real fix is token/supply side.

Acceptance criteria all met in PROGRESS.md §bf-2hdbg (lines 752-855). go vet + build + internal unit tests clean (docs change touches no Go code).
issue.title: Confirm migration window is the only thing accepting sim nodes

issue.description:
Split-child 1 of 3 for parent bf-53ut (Wrap each test in per-test setjmp/longjmp recovery so a failing assertion is non-fatal). This child installs the structural skeleton of the per-test recovery loop: it puts a setjmp(g_test_jmp) guard in front of the existing direct body call landed by sibling bf-1zew (run-command comment + naive registry iteration calling each g_tests[i].fn() directly), so that control returns here — rather than aborting — when a failed assertion inside the body calls test_record_failure() (which longjmp(g_test_jmp, 1) — sibling bf-3id).

Scope (extend firmware/test/test_runner.c, main()'s per-test loop):
- In main()'s loop, replace the bare g_tests[i].fn(); call with a guarded form: if (setjmp(g_test_jmp) == 0) { g_tests[i].fn(); }. On the DIRECT call setjmp returns 0 and the body runs as before; if the body trips test_record_failure(), the longjmp returns control to the setjmp call site with a non-zero value instead.
- On the non-zero (longjmp) return, do NOT re-invoke the body — leave the else branch empty (a bare comment is fine) for now. Just fall through so the loop advances to i+1. (Observability on the failure path lands in child 2; outcome PASS/FAIL labels land in a later sibling — do not add either here.)
- Either way the loop advances to the next i, so a failure in test N never blocks tests N+1..end. That per-test isolation is the whole point.

Implementation note (the classic setjmp trap — C11 7.13.2.1): any automatic variable modified between setjmp and longjmp AND read after the longjmp returns must be volatile-qualified, else its value is indeterminate. The loop index i is read in the post-longjmp path; confirm it is NOT modified between the setjmp call and the longjmp (it is only incremented by the for-loop increment, which runs AFTER control returns), so no volatile is needed. Record this reasoning in a comment next to the setjmp.

Acceptance criteria:
- main()'s loop calls setjmp(g_test_jmp) before each body and invokes g_tests[i].fn() ONLY on the 0 return; on a longjmp return it advances without re-calling.
- A comment near the setjmp records the volatile-analysis (i is not modified between setjmp and longjmp, so no volatile is needed).
- Compiles cleanly with gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra (no setjmp-related warnings).
- No changes to firmware/main/* or firmware/CMakeLists.txt.

The setjmp guard itself was already committed by an earlier single-pass bead (bf-bq9, in the file header), so this bead's incremental contribution is the volatile comment documenting that loop index i — read post-longjmp — is never modified between setjmp and longjmp (body only reads i; sole write is the for-loop increment after control returns), hence no volatile needed. Did NOT regress the pre-existing else-branch FAIL print, run summary, or non-zero exit code to a bare skeleton — those are committed bf-bq9 functionality the file header documents as the CI contract (make -C firmware/test test propagates non-zero on failure). Verified: clean gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra compile (zero warnings); recovery loop confirmed via a temp failing+passing test pair (failure longjmp'd, next test still ran and PASSED, exit non-zero); no firmware/main or CMakeLists changes.
