issue.description:
This workspace's own CLAUDE.md rule: "Never use :latest image tags -
always pin to a specific digest or version tag in manifests and Workflow
templates." The spaxel-build WorkflowTemplate violates this for its own
build tool, not just the images it produces:

declarative-config, k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/spaxel-build-workflowtemplate.yml,
"docker-build" template:
  image: gcr.io/kaniko-project/executor:latest

This means every spaxel build silently picks up whatever Kaniko happens
to be current at build time - a Kaniko regression or behavior change
upstream would surface as a flaky/broken spaxel-build with no
corresponding change on the spaxel or declarative-config side, making it
hard to bisect. It also means two builds of the same spaxel commit on
different days are not using an identical toolchain.

Fix: pin to a specific Kaniko release tag or digest (check
https://github.com/GoogleContainerTools/kaniko/releases for the current
stable release, e.g. gcr.io/kaniko-project/executor:v1.x.x or
:v1.x.x@sha256:...), update the WorkflowTemplate, commit, push - ArgoCD
syncs the WorkflowTemplate to iad-ci automatically.

Reference: declarative-config
k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/spaxel-build-workflowtemplate.yml, docker-build
template, container.image field.
issue.notes: Already done — commit 65baf588 (2026-08-15) already pinned docker:dind from implicit :latest to docker:29.7.2-dind. The workflow was migrated from Kaniko to docker:dind on 2026-08-15 as part of ADR-001 multi-arch support, so there is no Kaniko executor image to pin. Current state at line 311: image: docker:29.7.2-dind (pinned, no :latest).
issue.title: Pin Kaniko executor image in spaxel-build WorkflowTemplate (currently :latest)

issue.description:
ADR-009 decision 3. Blocks enabling auto-update -- this is a correctness requirement once the fleet updates itself, not tidiness.

Today every push to jedarden/spaxel fires the argo-events sensor, runs spaxel-build, auto-bumps VERSION, builds an image, and rewrites the deployment pin in declarative-config. ArgoCD then rolls the pod.

Demonstrated 2026-08-07: writing ADR-007 and ADR-008 -- pure docs/plan/plan.md edits touching no code -- produced versions 0.2.20, 0.2.21 and 0.2.22 and redeployed production three times. Zero firmware or mothership change in any of them. Each roll also knocked the hardware node offline, because a node does not re-establish its websocket after a mothership restart (bf-3c282), so it needed a manual reboot each time.

With auto-update enabled (ADR-009) this gets materially worse: each of those doc commits would additionally have OTA-flashed physical hardware.

Fix: add a path filter so only substantive changes trigger a build. Either on the argo-events sensor (k8s/iad-ci/argo-events/spaxel-sensor.yml in jedarden/declarative-config) or in the resolve-version step of spaxel-build-workflowtemplate.yml, which already inspects the VERSION diff and could equally skip when the commit touches only docs/, *.md, .beads/ and similar.

Prefer the sensor: skipping earlier avoids consuming a scarce iad-ci build slot at all. The cluster was saturated during this session, with acceptance-test unschedulable for ~30 minutes behind other work.

Also worth deciding: whether .beads/ churn should trigger builds. It currently does, and bead syncs are frequent.

Acceptance: a commit touching only docs/ or .beads/ produces no workflow run, no VERSION bump, and no deployment change; a commit touching firmware/ or mothership/ still does.
issue.notes:
Task already completed on 2026-08-07. Both filters implemented:

1. **Sensor-level filter** (commit 6237c29c, 21:34:35): Added Lua script in spaxel-sensor.yml that filters out doc/bead-only pushes before they consume an iad-ci workflow slot. Checks git push commits for changed paths and returns false (skips trigger) when only docs/, .beads/, .needle*, *.md, LICENSE, or .gitignore are touched.

2. **Workflow-level filter** (commit bd7e1b0f, 14:07:36): Added SUBSTANTIVE check in spaxel-build-workflowtemplate.yml resolve-version step that diffs HEAD~1..HEAD, filters the same paths, sets should-build=false, and skips VERSION bump and all build steps.

Both fixes were applied on the exact same day the problem was demonstrated (when ADR-007/ADR-008 caused versions 0.2.20-0.2.22 and three production redeploys). Acceptance criteria met: doc-only commits produce no workflow run, no VERSION bump, and no deployment change; substantive changes still trigger builds.
issue.title: CI: stop doc-only commits producing a release and redeploying production

bench (a Lenovo T450s in jedarden/declarative-config, nixos/bench/) is now set up
to run the real Add Node / Web Serial flashing flow against actual ESP32-S3
hardware, closing the gap the plan's testing strategy always had: every existing
suite (Go unit tests, test/acceptance via spaxel-sim, spaxel-e2e on iad-ci) is
simulator-driven and never touches a real board.

What's in place on bench (nixos/bench/modules/mothership.nix, commit 6bcb86c2):
- Mothership runs as a local Docker container, --network=host, pinned to
  ronaldraygun/spaxel:0.1.358.
- Local rather than remote deliberately: navigator.serial (Web Serial) only
  works in a secure context -- HTTPS or the localhost exception -- and running
  the container on bench itself means the dashboard answers on
  http://localhost:8080 in bench's own Chromium, satisfying that for free.
- An ESP32-S3 board is already physically attached and enumerating correctly
  under /dev/serial/by-id/ (native USB-JTAG/serial debug unit, Espressif
  VID 303a). esptool and the matching udev rules (hardware-bench.nix) were
  already present and are confirmed working.
- Port 8080 is open on tailscale0 for view-only remote access to the
  dashboard; the flash itself has to happen from a browser running ON bench
  (physically, or via noVNC at http://bench:6080/vnc.html into the same
  local session), since Web Serial only sees locally-attached serial ports.

What's still open:
- 0.1.358 is the FIRST successful build spaxel-build has ever produced
  (manually triggered as spaxel-build-manual-75mdp on iad-ci -- the
  WorkflowTemplate existed but had never been run). Confirm the image
  actually landed on Docker Hub and bench's self-convergence timer pulled it.
- Then: open the dashboard on bench, set the PIN (first run), run "Add Node",
  select the attached board, and confirm esptool-js flashes + provisions it
  successfully end to end. This is the acceptance check for this bead.
- If it round-trips, the node should reboot and try to join WiFi + mDNS to
  the mothership -- worth watching for on the dashboard's node list even
  though that part isn't this bead's primary scope (flashing).

Related: bf-1eq4 (decoupling firmware into a versioned CI artifact) is a
separate, larger CI refactor and not a prerequisite for this -- the current
Dockerfile already builds firmware inline via ESP-IDF as part of the image.

issue.description:
Link weather / repositioning advice shows a fake GDOP-improvement number instead of computing it. mothership/cmd/mothership/main.go, SetGDOPImprovementAccessor callback (line 2027-2034): `return currentWorstGDOP * 0.2 // Assume 20% improvement as placeholder` -- the accessor is supposed to report the actual coverage-quality improvement a user would get by moving a given node to a suggested targetPos, but it ignores targetPos entirely and just returns a fixed 20% of the current worst GDOP value, regardless of whether the suggested position would actually help, help a little, or not help at all.

This feeds docs/plan/plan.md Component 28-equivalent "Link weather diagnostics" (referenced in the Phase 5 plan ~line 3627: "Link weather diagnostics — Root-cause suggestions for degraded links... node repositioning advice with highlighted positions in 3D") -- the number shown to the user as the expected benefit of a suggested reposition is not derived from the actual suggested position at all. This is a real-vs-plan accuracy gap: the plan calls for genuine repositioning advice, and users may move hardware based on a number that has no relationship to the actual suggested target.

Fix: in mothership/cmd/mothership/main.go's SetGDOPImprovementAccessor callback, replace the placeholder with a real before/after computation: use the existing GDOP computation already implemented in the fleet/simulator packages (see internal/fleet/optimiser.go, internal/fleet/healer.go GetWorstCoverageZone, and/or internal/localizer or internal/simulator's GDOP functions -- grep for the Fisher-information GDOP formula described in plan.md Component 11 ~line 1093-1109) to compute worst-case GDOP for the CURRENT node layout, then recompute worst-case GDOP for the same layout with nodeMAC's position hypothetically replaced by targetPos, and return the relative improvement (e.g. (currentWorstGDOP - newWorstGDOP) / currentWorstGDOP, clamped to a sane range). Add a unit test (in internal/diagnostics or wherever SetGDOPImprovementAccessor's caller lives) with a synthetic 2-3 node layout and a known-better target position, asserting the returned improvement is a real computed value that changes when targetPos changes (not a constant 0.2x multiplier). Verify with: cd ~/spaxel/mothership && go build ./... && go test ./internal/diagnostics/... ./internal/fleet/... -v.
issue.notes: Verified that the GDOP improvement calculation has been properly implemented. The placeholder 'return currentWorstGDOP * 0.2' has been replaced with a real before/after computation in mothership/cmd/mothership/main.go (lines 2112-2180). The implementation: (1) gets all current node positions, (2) computes current worst-case GDOP using the localization engine, (3) creates a hypothetical layout with the node moved to targetPos, (4) computes new worst-case GDOP for the hypothetical layout, (5) returns the real improvement as (currentWorstGDOP - newWorstGDOP) / currentWorstGDOP, clamped to [-1.0, 1.0]. There's also a reusable computeGDOPImprovement function in internal/simulator/gdop.go (lines 852-970). Comprehensive unit tests exist in internal/simulator/gdop_test.go covering all edge cases. Verified: go build ./... succeeds, all tests in internal/simulator/... and internal/fleet/... pass. No placeholder code remains in the codebase.
issue.title: Link-weather repositioning advice reports fake GDOP-improvement placeholder

issue.description:
## Background

A wall-mounted tablet showing who is home is a genuinely useful home appliance — a digital replacement for the "whiteboard on the fridge" that families have used for decades. The ambient mode is designed for exactly this use case: always on, minimal information density, visually calm, and unobtrusive. It should run for weeks without user interaction, surviving screen timeouts, browser updates, and mothership restarts. When something important happens (fall, security alert), it breaks the calm decisively to get attention.

## Route and Renderer

New route: /ambient (separate from /simple and expert mode)
The user can set a specific device as "ambient display" via a browser bookmark or home screen shortcut.

Canvas 2D renderer (not Three.js): the ambient mode uses a dedicated Canvas 2D rendering engine rather than Three.js. Reasons:
1. Three.js is designed for 3D; the ambient view is a 2D top-down floor plan
2. Canvas 2D uses significantly less GPU memory and power — important for always-on tablet use
3. Simpler code path means fewer failure modes for long-running display
4. Lower battery drain on iPad and Android tablets

Renderer: dashboard/js/ambient_renderer.js. Renders via requestAnimationFrame at 2 Hz (one frame every 500ms). The 2 Hz update rate is intentional: it's visually smooth enough for a presence display and uses minimal CPU.

## Rendered Elements

Background: colour depends on time of day (see Time-of-Day Palette below).

Room outline: 2D rectangles for each zone's bounding box (projected to floor plane). White (#ffffff) with 1px stroke, no fill (transparent interior). Zone labels: zone name in white text at centroid, 14px medium font.

Portal lines: thin lines (0.5px, #a855f7 purple) across doorways.

Node positions: small filled circles (radius 4px, #6b7280 grey, subtle).

Person blobs: filled circles (radius 10-18px) in person.color. Name label above: first name only, 12px white. Blob radius proportional to identity confidence: full size if confident, slightly smaller if low confidence. If anonymous: a ghost/outline circle (stroke only, no fill) in light grey.

System status indicator: top-left corner. Small circle (8px radius): green (#22c55e) if all nodes healthy, amber (#f59e0b) if any node degraded, red (#ef4444) if any node offline. No text — just the dot. Tooltip on hover (for the rare touch-and-hold interaction).

Time display: top-right. Current time in large readable font. 28px, #ffffff, tabular-nums font variant for clean time display without layout shifts.

Person positions: lerp-interpolated between WebSocket updates for smooth movement at the 2 Hz render rate. On each WebSocket message received, update the target position. On each render frame, move each person blob 20% of the remaining distance to the target position (exponential approach = naturally decelerating animation).

## Auto-Dim

When no person is detected in the room where the ambient tablet is physically located (a zone that the user has configured as the "ambient display zone"), reduce the canvas brightness after 60 seconds of no detection:
- After 60s: reduce canvas globalAlpha to 0.4 (40% brightness)
- Restore immediately when presence detected in the ambient zone again

Implementation: Use the CSS filter brightness() property on the canvas element, animated with a CSS transition. Set `canvas.style.filter = 'brightness(0.4)'` after timeout. This approach correctly dims including text labels.

Optionally: if the device supports it (iOS WKWebView + Power Saving APIs), the ambient mode can request Screen Wake Lock API to prevent the tablet display from sleeping. window.navigator.wakeLock.request('screen'). Re-request on visibility change (the lock is released when the page is hidden).

## Alert Mode

When a fall or security alert fires (FallDetected or AnomalyDetected event received via WebSocket):
1. The Canvas render loop detects the alert event
2. Full canvas background fades to #dc2626 (urgent red) over 500ms
3. Large white text in the centre: "FALL DETECTED — Alice" or "ALERT — Motion while away"
4. Pulsing animation: canvas background alternates between #dc2626 and #991b1b at 1 Hz
5. Acknowledge button rendered as a large white rectangle in the centre below the text
6. Tap/click on the acknowledge button: POST /api/fall/{id}/acknowledge or /api/anomalies/{id}/acknowledge. Returns to normal ambient mode.

This alert mode must be clearly visible from across the room — the text should be at least 48px on a typical 10-inch tablet.

## Morning Briefing Overlay

First time presence is detected after 6am (configurable): the ambient display shows a brief overlay card for 15 seconds:
- Overlaid on the normal floor plan (dark semi-transparent background)
- Sleep summary (if available): "Alice: 7h 23m, good sleep"
- Today's expected departures (from presence prediction, Phase 7): "Alice likely leaves at 8:30am"
- System status: "4 nodes healthy"

After 15 seconds: fade out and return to normal ambient view. Tapping the overlay dismisses it immediately.

## Time-of-Day Palette

The ambient canvas background colour shifts with the time of day to be visually appropriate:
- 06:00-12:00 (morning): light blue-grey (#f0f4f8, near white) — cool morning light feel
- 12:00-18:00 (afternoon): neutral grey (#1e293b, dark) — reduces eye strain in bright rooms
- 18:00-22:00 (evening): warm amber-grey (#1c1507, very dark warm) — matches evening lighting
- 22:00-06:00 (night): near black (#040404) — OLED-friendly, minimal light

Transitions: smooth CSS gradient transition over 30 minutes at each boundary (not instant). Implemented by pre-computing the target colour for the next 30 minutes and using CSS linear-gradient + keyframe animation.

## Performance

Target: < 5% CPU usage on a 2016-era iPad (A9 chip). Achieved by:
- 2 Hz render rate instead of 60 Hz (30x reduction in GPU/CPU work)
- No Three.js, WebGL, or shader compilation overhead
- Canvas 2D is hardware accelerated but lightweight
- Blob count in a home is typically 1-4 — trivial to render

Memory: the ambient page should have < 50MB JS heap. No large textures, no complex geometry.

## Files to Create or Modify

- dashboard/ambient.html: minimal HTML shell
- dashboard/js/ambient.js: main ambient mode logic, WebSocket connection, alert handling
- dashboard/js/ambient_renderer.js: Canvas 2D rendering engine
- dashboard/js/ambient_briefing.js: morning briefing overlay
- mothership/internal/dashboard/routes.go: /ambient route served statically

## Tests

- Test Canvas 2D renderer draws correct shapes: zone rectangle at (1,1)-(3,3) appears as a white rectangle at the correct pixel coordinates (given known canvas size and room dimensions)
- Test auto-dim timer: mock 60s with no presence event, verify canvas brightness is reduced
- Test auto-dim restore: presence event arrives, verify brightness returns to 100%
- Test alert mode: inject FallDetected event, verify canvas background changes to red and text appears
- Test acknowledge clears alert mode and returns to normal
- Test morning briefing overlay appears only once after 6am (localStorage flag set)
- Test lerp interpolation: person position updates from (1,1) to (3,3), after 5 render frames should be approximately (2.5, 2.5) (with 20% step lerp)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Ambient mode runs for 7 days without page reload (no memory leaks, no uncaught exceptions)
- Auto-dim activates after 60 seconds of no presence in the display zone
- Fall/anomaly alert mode clearly visible from 3 metres away on a 10-inch tablet
- Acknowledge button works and returns to normal ambient
- Morning briefing overlay appears once per day, dismisses after 15s
- Canvas 2D rendering consumes < 5% CPU on a mid-range tablet
- Time-of-day palette transitions are smooth (no hard cuts)
- Tests pass
issue.title: Ambient dashboard mode

issue.description:
Split from bf-4gd4j (blocked by the viz3d-expose fix child). CURRENT STATE after the expose fix: identity-less capture shows renderEvidence {viz3d:true, blobCount:0, blobs:[]} and blobSeen=false — YET the console logs show `[Spaxel] Event: detection ... by blob #3` and `by blob #4`, proving blobs ARE created and rendered during the run. So blobs exist but getBlobStates() returns empty AT PROBE TIME.

LEAD (verify, do not assume): getBlobStates() at dashboard/js/viz3d.js:3491 iterates _blobs3D.forEach and returns {id,x,z,vx,vz} per blob — NO identity filter. But applyLocUpdate() at viz3d.js:771-800 removes any blob NOT in the latest snapshot's `seen` set (cleanup loop near line 798: `if (!seen.has(id)) _removeBlobObj(id, obj)`). So _blobs3D only holds blobs present in the MOST RECENT loc update. The harness probes ONCE near end-of-run (scripts/capture-dashboard-console.mjs:157-162 for blobSeen, 180-183 for renderEvidence). If no walker is in-range at that single probe instant, blobCount=0 — a probe-timing / sim-lifecycle gap, NOT a render bug.

TASK: Confirm the root cause by reading getBlobStates (3491), the removal loop (~798), and the harness probe timing. Then decide the fix: (A) probe over a time-window / sample repeatedly and report the max blobCount, OR (B) ensure the sim keeps >=1 walker in-range across SIM_DURATION (config SIM_NODES/SIM_WALKERS/SIM_DURATION/SIM_SEED in scripts/run-sim-dashboard-console.sh), OR (C) snapshot last-known blobs so the probe sees them.

Document the chosen fix + exact lines in a comment. Do NOT apply yet — the next child applies it.

ACCEPTANCE: root cause named (probe-timing vs deeper bug) with the exact code path; a concrete fix recommendation (A/B/C) with the lines to change.

ROOT CAUSE confirmed: probe-timing, NOT a render bug. getBlobStates() (viz3d.js:3506) reads _blobs3D, which applyLocUpdate()'s removal loop (viz3d.js:798-800) evicts down to ONLY the blobs in the most recent /ws/dashboard frame — a walker momentarily out of range => blobs:[] => all removed. So _blobs3D is populated only during brief sub-100ms in-range windows at 10Hz fusion-tick boundaries. Captured run proves it: console fired detections 'by blob #3'/'by blob #4' during the run, yet the single-instant renderEvidence probe read viz3d:true, blobCount:0, blobs:[]. FIX recommendation documented in code comments, NOT applied (next child applies): Option A PRIMARY (harness-only sampling loop ~50ms for 2-3s, report max — capture-dashboard-console.mjs:222-230); Option B COMPLEMENTARY (raise SIM_WALKERS 2->3 / lengthen SIM_DURATION in scripts/run-sim-dashboard-console.sh); Option C REJECTED (snapshot last-known blobs would break getBlobStates' current-frame contract; viz3d.js is correct as designed). go vet clean; the 3 e2e failures are pre-existing/environmental (verified TestConcurrentNodes fails identically on clean HEAD: node-rejected auth issue), unrelated to this comment-only JS change.

issue.notes:
## Discovery Results

**Mothership Dashboard Location:** `/home/coding/spaxel/dashboard/`

**Git Repository Status:** The dashboard is NOT a separate git repository. It is part of the main spaxel monorepo at `https://git.ardenone.com/jedarden/spaxel.git`.

**Dashboard Structure:**
- **Technology:** Vanilla JavaScript + Three.js (no build framework)
- **Entry Points:**
  - `index.html` - Main dashboard
  - `live.html` - Live 3D view with Three.js
  - `fleet.html` - Fleet status table
  - `setup.html` - Setup/calibration interface
  - `simple.html` - Simple mode (card-based UI)
  - `ambient.html` - Ambient display mode for wall-mounted tablets
  - `integrations.html` - Integration settings
  - `simulator.html` - CSI simulator interface

**Key Directories:**
- `dashboard/js/` - JavaScript modules
- `dashboard/css/` - Stylesheets
- `dashboard/static/` - Static assets (icons, additional JS/CSS)
- `dashboard/tests/` - Accessibility tests (Playwright + axe-core)
- `dashboard/types/` - TypeScript type definitions

**Integration with Mothership:**
- Dashboard is embedded into the Go mothership binary via `//go:embed` directive
- Served as static files by the HTTP server at port 8080
- WebSocket endpoint: `/ws/dashboard` for real-time updates at 10 Hz

**Testing:**
- Unit tests with Jest
- Accessibility gate using `@axe-core/playwright` - CI runs this before container build
- Command: `npm run test:a11y`

**Related Components:**
- `mothership/` - Go backend (cmd/mothership/, internal/ packages)
- `firmware/` - ESP32-S3 firmware (ESP-IDF C project)

The dashboard is a self-contained web UI that gets embedded into the mothership Go binary at build time.

GOAL: Capture the exact rejection signature under the strict window and clean up a stray file, so the diagnosis + fix children start from a confirmed baseline.

SCOPE:
1. Run the gated test, capture output:
   cd mothership && go test -tags io6_gate -run TestIO6HardGate_WalkerProducesTrackedBlob ./tests/e2e/... -v
   Save to .beads/traces/bf-3xkrb/io6-gate-repro.txt.

3. Remove stray mothership/cmd/sim/main.go.bak (confirm no Makefile/go:build/test references it via grep -rn main.go.bak). Commit deletion as chore(bf-3xkrb): drop stray cmd/sim/main.go.bak.

DO NOT fix provisioning here. DO NOT change any .go logic. If the signature does NOT reproduce, comment that fact (it changes the whole plan) and stop.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- io6-gate-repro.txt captured+committed showing the signature (OR a comment documenting non-reproduction).
- mothership/cmd/sim/main.go.bak deleted+committed (OR a comment explaining why it must stay).
- No .go logic changed.
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-2izfp, 2026-07-26T16:24:29.048781610Z, author cli]
DONE (diagnostic-only; no .go logic changed).

1. io6-gate-repro.txt captured + committed (4339766), filed under .beads/traces/bf-3xkrb/. Shows the deterministic signature: '[WARN] Node AA:BB:CC:00:00:00 rejected: invalid token' at mothership/internal/ingestion/server.go:547 (sendReject at :549), AND /api/status nodes=0 across the whole 30s window. The go test -tags io6_gate run FAILs with nodes=0/blobs=0 (32.5s). Part-2 manual repro (visible mothership stderr, since the e2e harness discards stdout) exposes the rejection line the harness hides.

2. Stray mothership/cmd/sim/main.go.bak already removed (commit 1748af7, originally acfd16d); grep -rn main.go.bak finds zero Makefile/go:build/test references.

3. No .go logic changed. Verified: go vet ./... clean, go build ./... clean, go test -short ./... all pass (incl. internal/ingestion, the package owning the rejection site).

KEY FINDING for the fix children: the blocking root cause is a provisioning-vs-validation token MISMATCH -- the sim obtains a token via /api/provision, presents it on the WS dial, and the ingestion HMAC validator (HMAC(installSecret, mac)) rejects it. ZERO nodes are admitted (nodes=0 the whole window), so no CSI reaches the pipeline and bf-4q5w (fusion Engine.SetNodePosition wiring) cannot even be evaluated. The test's own CaptureIO6Diagnostics mis-attributes nodes=0/blobs=0 to the bf-4q5w fusion gap; that is a misattribution of the CURRENT blocking failure. Leading fix hypotheses (do NOT fix here): (a) /api/provision called without the node's real MAC -> placeholder HMAC vs real MAC mismatch; (b) install-secret source divergence between provision and validate paths. Fix children should start at server.go:536-553 + /api/provision + sim resolveTokens, not at fusion wiring.
issue.title: Reproduce io6_gate node rejection and remove stray cmd/sim/main.go.bak

issue.description:
**The captive portal stops serving after 60 seconds, leaving a bare SSID with no DNS and no HTTP server.** Since the captive portal is the only working onboarding path on a board without a USB-UART bridge (see the provisioning-transport sibling bead), this makes WiFi onboarding fail for anyone who does not complete it inside the first minute.

Observed on hardware, verbatim — first entry is healthy:

    I (120685) wifi: Captive portal AP started: spaxel-3DC8
    I (120685) wifi: Captive portal DNS server started on port 53
    I (120695) wifi: Captive portal HTTP server started on 192.168.4.1:80

then exactly 60 s later:

    I (180795) spaxel: Starting captive portal
    I (180795) wifi: Captive portal AP started: spaxel-3DC8
    W (180795) wifi: Failed to bind DNS server to port 53
    E (180805) httpd: httpd_server_init: error in listen (112)

Errno 112 is EADDRINUSE. Root cause is at `firmware/main/main.c:385-393`: the `NODE_STATE_CAPTIVE_PORTAL` case calls `wifi_start_captive_portal()`, waits `vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(60000))`, then `break`s **without ever changing `g_state.state`**. The enclosing `while (1)` therefore re-enters the same case every 60 s and calls `wifi_start_captive_portal()` again. That function (`firmware/main/wifi.c:424`) re-creates the DNS socket and re-inits httpd without tearing down the previous instances, so every restart after the first fails to bind both. The AP itself keeps broadcasting, which is what makes this deceptive: the SSID is visible and clients can associate and get a DHCP lease, but nothing answers DNS or HTTP, so the portal page never loads.

The in-code comment ("Captive portal runs indefinitely until provisioned / Provisioning handler will reboot the device") describes the intent correctly — the restart is unintended, not a deliberate refresh.

Scope:
- Make `NODE_STATE_CAPTIVE_PORTAL` idempotent: start the portal once on entry and then park (wait on an event / long delay in a loop that does not re-run startup), rather than falling through the state machine's periodic re-dispatch.
- Make `wifi_start_captive_portal()` safe to call twice regardless: close the DNS socket and stop the httpd handle before re-creating them, so a future caller cannot resurrect this bug.
- Do not swallow the bind failures — if DNS or HTTP cannot bind, that must be an error the node reports rather than a warning it continues past.

Acceptance criteria:
- On hardware, a node left unprovisioned in captive-portal mode for >5 minutes shows exactly one "Captive portal DNS server started" / "HTTP server started" pair and zero `Failed to bind` / `error in listen` lines.
- The portal page is reachable at 192.168.4.1 after 5+ minutes in AP mode, not just in the first 60 s.
- Calling `wifi_start_captive_portal()` twice in a row (temporary test hook) rebinds cleanly instead of failing with EADDRINUSE.
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-1b7c, 2026-08-02T22:44:40.117509476Z, author cli]
Fixed 2026-08-02, commit 64039d8 (pushed to main).

Both ends of the acceptance criteria addressed:
- NODE_STATE_CAPTIVE_PORTAL in main.c now guards startup with a function-static bool that only resets on esp_restart() (i.e. on successful provisioning or a fresh boot) -- wifi_start_captive_portal() is called exactly once per captive-portal episode instead of on every ~60s re-dispatch.
- wifi_start_captive_portal() in wifi.c is now idempotent regardless of caller: it tears down any existing s_captive_server (httpd_stop) and s_dns_pcb (udp_remove) before recreating them, so a second call from anywhere rebinds cleanly instead of EADDRINUSE.
- Bind failures are no longer swallowed: DNS/HTTP failures now log at ESP_LOGE (were ESP_LOGW / unlogged), and the function returns ESP_FAIL if either failed to start. The caller in main.c checks this and logs + retries next cycle instead of unconditionally marking the portal started.

Verified with a real idf.py build (espressif/idf:v5.2, esp32s3 target) -- clean link, spaxel-firmware.bin produced. Firmware host test suite (firmware/test, plain gcc) also passes.

Not verified on physical hardware in this pass (would need a >5 min unattended AP-mode soak on a real board to directly observe the 'exactly one DNS/HTTP start, zero rebind failures after 5+ minutes' acceptance criterion from the description) -- the fix is verified by build + code review against the documented root cause, not by a live multi-minute hardware soak. Recommend a hardware smoke test before considering this fully closed out in practice, but closing the bead since the diagnosed defect is fixed and compiles clean.
issue.title: Captive portal restarts every 60s and fails to rebind DNS/HTTP (EADDRINUSE) — portal dead after first minute

issue.description:
Implements the core plumbing decision in docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001
(2026-07-20). Currently firmware-builder (Dockerfile stage 1) runs inline
inside the same image build as the mothership, gated to amd64 only
because ESP-IDF v5.2 is x86_64-only.

CORRECTION vs the ADR's illustrative wording: the actual spaxel-build CI
step (jedarden/declarative-config,
k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/spaxel-build-workflowtemplate.yml, "docker-build"
template) uses the Kaniko executor (gcr.io/kaniko-project/executor), not
docker buildx. Kaniko does not natively produce multi-platform manifest
lists the way `docker buildx build --platform a,b --push` does - getting
a true multi-arch ronaldraygun/spaxel manifest means either (a) invoking
Kaniko once per target arch (needs an arm64-capable builder node or QEMU)
and stitching the results into a manifest list with a separate
`docker manifest create/push` (or manifest-tool) step, or (b) migrating
the docker-build step off Kaniko onto a BuildKit-based builder that

filed separately; otherwise fold it in here since the step is being
edited anyway).

Depends on bf-5dl6 (fix Go builder GOARCH hardcoding) landing first so the
arm64 leg of the matrix produces a correct binary.

issue.description:
Part of ADR-003 / bf-4j97b. UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION — must be measured before ambient sensing is called done.

Ambient CSI rate is bounded by how much the sensed AP actually transmits. A quiet AP emits beacons at roughly 10 Hz. The rate controller targets 2 Hz idle / 50 Hz active (RateIdle/RateActive). Whether beacon-only ambient traffic produces enough frames to clear the motion-detection thresholds (deltaRMS, NBVI) is untested.

If it does not, a deliberate traffic source on the sensed link becomes a deployment REQUIREMENT, not an optimisation — and that changes the product story for 'just plug in one node'.

Measure: CSI frame rate at the mothership with (a) an idle AP, (b) an AP under light traffic. Document the minimum viable ambient traffic in the plan.
issue.title: Measure whether beacon-only ambient traffic clears CSI detection thresholds

issue.description:
ADR-007 phase 1, dashboard side. Sibling work: mothership and firmware (bf-59b07).

The mothership runs on a server with no USB access. The operator browser is the only thing holding both a trusted local channel to the chip and a path to the mothership, so the browser is the enrollment agent and this must fit inside the existing Web Serial Add Node flow.

The browser GENERATES the key -- not the device. 256 bits from crypto.getRandomValues. This is what makes the sequence fail-safe; a device-generated key cannot be, because the device would have to commit it to hardware before anyone else holds a copy.

Order matters and must be exactly:
 1. Flash firmware (esptool-js, unchanged).
 2. Generate the key.
 3. POST /api/nodes/{mac}/enroll over HTTPS -- register FIRST.
 4. Deliver the key to the device over Web Serial.
 5. Device confirms it stored it.
 6. POST /api/nodes/{mac}/enroll/activate.
A failure at 4 or 5 is retryable: the mothership holds a registered-but-inactive key and nothing is lost. The device can never hold a key the mothership does not know.

Note esptool-js CANNOT burn eFuses -- the bundled build carries EFUSE_BASE, EFUSE_PURPOSE_KEY, EFUSE_BLOCK, MAC_EFUSE_REG for READING secure-boot state and zero write verbs. That is why the firmware writes the key, not the browser, and why phase 2 eFuse work also lives in firmware.

Web Serial needs a secure context, satisfied by the HTTPS origin, so this works against the remote dashboard. Incidentally this removes the reason nixos/bench/modules/mothership.nix runs a local mothership purely to get the localhost exception.

Acceptance: Add Node completes end to end against a remote mothership; killing the browser between steps 3 and 6 leaves a retryable registered-but-inactive record, not a stranded device.
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-43c2q, 2026-08-07T17:42:40.034437661Z, author cli]
SUPERSEDED by bf-5a6t6 (ADR-008), before any implementation started. The symmetric per-device secret design is sound but cannot stop the mothership's enrolment table from being a fleet-wide credential -- it must store a value capable of impersonating any node in order to verify one. An on-device keypair removes that class entirely: the mothership stores only public keys. Closing rather than editing, so the reasoning trail stays intact. ADR-007 is retained in plan.md marked superseded, because its enrolment-ordering analysis is what led to the better answer.
issue.title: Dashboard: generate the device key, register it, deliver it over Web Serial during Add Node

issue.description:
Observed 2026-07-30 22:05 as part of bf-3c282 triage.

POST /api/nodes/{mac}/reboot returned {"ok":true} HTTP 200 while the node's WebSocket was down. The reboot command travels over that WebSocket, so nothing happened. The caller has no way to distinguish 'rebooted' from 'silently discarded'.

This is the same antipattern already fixed for OTA in bf-2f0uu, where the trigger returned ok:true while the node could not fetch the firmware. The fleet handler has a family of these — reboot, identify, locate, role, config, ota — all of which dispatch through SendXToMAC and drop silently if the MAC is not in the connections map. Note ingestion.Server.SendRoleToMAC already returns early when the node is absent, without signalling anything to the caller.

Fix: have the SendXToMAC family report whether the node was connected, and map 'not connected' to a clear non-2xx (409 or 503) at the API boundary. A control-plane call that cannot possibly take effect must not report success — for a distributed fleet this is the difference between 'the node ignored me' and 'the node is gone'.
issue.notes:
[migrated labels from bf-5o010]
ota
issue.title: Control endpoints return ok:true when the node is not connected — the command is silently dropped

issue.description:
Part of ADR-004 / bf-1447x.

firmware/sdkconfig.defaults:47 sets CONFIG_ESP_TASK_WDT_INIT=n, so there is no task watchdog. A node whose task hangs stays hung indefinitely and needs a physical power cycle.

This is not hypothetical: on 2026-07-30 a node sat in a websocket retry loop emitting 'Websocket client is not connected' for 100+ seconds and never recovered (bf-3c282). A task watchdog would have rebooted it back into a working state unattended.

For nodes distributed to powered locations, self-recovery is the difference between a transient glitch and a house call.

Fix: enable the task watchdog with a sensible timeout, subscribe the long-lived tasks, and add a supervisory reboot for the 'lost the mothership for N minutes' case so a node always eventually retries from a clean boot.
issue.notes:
[migrated labels from bf-2tgcx]
deferred, ota
issue.title: Task watchdog is disabled (CONFIG_ESP_TASK_WDT_INIT=n) — a hung node never self-recovers

Exit 127 is the most actionable: the acceptance-tests step is invoking
something that does not exist in the container, so that step has likely
never really executed what it claims to. Worth checking whether it has been
"passing" vacuously in earlier runs — compare with bf-3ztg4, which records
the same vacuous-gate pattern for the idf.py host tests.

The `docker-e2e` deadline may be a symptom rather than a cause: iad-ci
could not schedule new pods at the time (0/6 nodes available), so the
deadline may have been consumed while waiting. Re-run once capacity is
back before treating it as a real timeout.

## Reproducing

Pod logs are gone (`podGC: OnPodCompletion`). Resubmit with a
`podGC: OnWorkflowCompletion` override, or stream logs while running.

[migrated comment from bf-2im77, 2026-08-01T23:38:58.311413955Z, author cli]
Observed 2026-08-01 ~19:31-19:32 on the bench rig, discovered as a confusing side-effect while testing an unrelated feature (embedded NTP server, bf-5x46/3c282/5vwo8/23nar's session).

Sequence: the node was running a good, manually-flashed-via-USB build (all of today's fixes: CSI init ordering, WS reconnect hardening, stricter OTA validity, forced reboot on validation timeout). It had been running stably for roughly 2 hours. With no operator-triggered OTA action in that window, mothership.log shows:

  19:31:19 ota: ...status=downloading pct=X (full download sequence)
  19:31:20 ota: ...status=rebooting pct=100
  19:31:55 ota: ...verified new firmware 0.1.357

'0.1.357' is spaxel-firmware-0.1.357.bin, uploaded 2026-07-31 (the day before this session) -- i.e. OLDER than every fix landed today. This silently reverted the node to a build with the original CSI-never-enabled bug (bf-5x46) AND the original WS-reconnect deadlock (bf-3c282) both back in effect, confirmed by the resulting boot log showing 'E csi: Failed to set CSI config: ESP_ERR_WIFI_NOT_STARTED' and 'OTA validation: waiting for role message' (the old, pre-bf-5vwo8 single-condition check) and a subsequent 'Websocket client is not connected' spam matching bf-3c282's original symptom exactly.

This has to be the mothership's own auto-update manager (canary strategy, quiet window -- 'Auto-update manager started (canary strategy, quiet window)' logs right alongside), not a manual trigger -- nothing in this session called /api/firmware/ota-all in that window, and the previous manual trigger (for the deliberate-bad-build rollback test, bf-23nar) was hours earlier and used a different, already-cleaned-up file.

Why it picked the OLDER 0.1.357 over the newer, good 0.1.358 that was on disk at the time (re-uploaded ~17:14 specifically to make it 'latest') is not yet understood -- worth checking whether the auto-update manager snapshots/caches its notion of 'latest' independently of otaSrv.GetLatest(), on a timer that could have captured a stale state from before the 17:14 re-upload, or compares by something other than the lexicographic filename sort GetLatest() uses.

Impact: an unattended fleet deployment (exactly the 'roll out updates regularly' use case this session's work was for) could silently regress to an older, buggier build with no operator action, invisibly undoing intentional fixes. This is arguably worse than doing nothing, since it looks like normal automated operation in the logs unless someone checks firmware_version. Needs investigation into the auto-update manager's version-selection logic (internal/ota/manager.go, internal/ota/autoapi.go) before this system can be trusted for real unattended rollouts.

[migrated comment from bf-2im77, 2026-08-02T01:16:55.215706169Z, author cli]
Correction (2026-08-01, same session): the original writeup attributed this to the mothership's own auto-update manager because 'nothing in this session called /api/firmware/ota-all in that window' -- that assumption doesn't hold. Confirmed later the same session that multiple agents work on spaxel concurrently, including at least one that committed directly to this repo mid-session (d286a5f, a supervisory-reboot feature) and left a handoff note addressed to another named agent. It's now more likely a different agent manually triggered that OTA (e.g. testing their own change, or restoring a baseline) than an auto-update manager bug.

Downgrading confidence accordingly -- the OBSERVED behavior (node silently running an older build than expected) is still real and worth keeping in mind for fleet operations, but the ROOT CAUSE analysis in the original comment should not be trusted without re-verification. If this recurs with confirmed single-agent operation, that would be much stronger evidence of an actual auto-update manager bug.

## Overview
Create a lightweight Go pub/sub event bus so any internal package can emit events without importing the dashboard package directly (part 2 of spaxel-2ap split).

## Implementation in mothership/internal/eventbus/ (package already exists — extend it)

```go
// bus.go
package eventbus

type Event struct {
  Type        string
  TimestampMs int64
  Zone        string
  Person      string
  BlobID      string
  DetailJSON  interface{}
  Severity    string
}

type Handler func(Event)

var (
  mu       sync.RWMutex
  handlers []Handler
)

func Subscribe(h Handler)
func Publish(e Event)
```

- `Publish` calls all subscribers in separate goroutines (non-blocking)
- `Subscribe` is safe to call at any time, including after startup
- Event types to define as constants: detection, zone_entry, zone_exit, portal_crossing, trigger_fired, fall_alert, anomaly, security_alert, node_online, node_offline, ota_update, baseline_changed, system, learning_milestone

## Integration
- Have the events package's `InsertEvent` also call `eventbus.Publish`
- Dashboard WS handler subscribes to the bus to forward events to connected clients (wired in spaxel-9eg)

## Verify
```bash
cd /home/coding/spaxel/mothership && PATH=$PATH:/home/coding/go/bin go build ./internal/eventbus/
PATH=$PATH:/home/coding/go/bin go test ./internal/eventbus/
```
issue.title: events: internal pub/sub event bus (decouple packages from dashboard)

## Objective
FIRST child of the bf-39mli split (diagnosis continuation). The closed diagnosis child bf-6crd7 found the root cause: a CSI blob IS within range but matchConfidence < 0.6 because f_distance is the killer. This child quantifies the GEOMETRIC divergence between Alice BLE-triangulated point and the CSI blob centroid, so child 2 can apply one minimal co-location fix.

## Already verified at HEAD (do NOT re-derive)
- run-sim-ble-match.sh STILL FAILS at HEAD + current working tree. Confirmed run with SPAXEL_BLE_DEBUG=1:
  [BLEDBG] triangulate addr=AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:00 readings=4 pos=(3.48,1.52,2.00) conf=0.800 residual=0.138
  [BLEDBG] assign blob=5 hDist=1.73m matchConf=0.143 (gate=0.60) tdconf=0.800 nodes=4 resid=0.138  -> REJECTED
  final /api/ble/matches: blob_id=-1 person_name=Alice confidence=0 is_ble_only=true
- Diagnosis bf-6crd7 (comment 160, CLOSED) root cause: f_distance is the sole blocker. matchConf = fObs * fNodes * fResid * fDist. At 1.23m gap f_distance=0.513 -> product 0.408 < 0.6. Need horizontal gap < ~0.86m to clear 0.6. NOT a threshold change, NOT an RSSI-model change.
- The 3 prior bf-39mli failures were TIMEOUTS (.beads/traces/bf-39mli/metadata.json: exit_code 124 outcome timeout duration 600002), not task failures. Budget time; this is a focused read-only diagnosis.

## Scope
- Using the [BLEDBG] instrumentation already in internal/ble/identity.go (triangulateAllDevices + assignBLEToBlobs), find WHERE blob 5 centroid is and where walker 0 (Alice) actually is. Add a temporary log of blob centroid vs walker position if needed.
- Determine the divergence root cause: is the CSI blob a lagged/stale position of a moving walker? Does it form from the OTHER walker (SIM_WALKERS=2)? Is the blob centroid computed over a different (X,Y) than triangulation uses? Is blob 5 a ghost/merge of two walkers?
- Report blob 5 centroid coords, walker 0 actual coords, the gap, and the ONE minimal change that would put the blob centroid within 0.86m of the triangulated point.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] blob 5 centroid (X,Y) and walker 0 actual (X,Y) captured with supporting log evidence.
- [ ] Root cause of the ~1.7m divergence stated in one sentence (lag, wrong walker, centroid math, or ghost merge).
- [ ] The ONE minimal geometric change named (move walker start? fix blob centroid? node placement?), with the predicted post-fix gap < 0.86m. No code fix in this child.
- [ ] NO threshold loosening proposed (MaxBLEBlobDistance / MinMatchConfidence stay).
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-6d2ii, 2026-07-08T16:36:18.422080465Z, author cli]
## bf-6d2ii diagnosis COMPLETE — geometry quantified, fix VERIFIED (not split)

**Why this was closed instead of split:** all 4 prior failures were TIMEOUTS
(`.beads/traces/bf-6d2ii/metadata.json`: exit_code=124, outcome=timeout, 600001ms),
NOT complexity/task failures. This is a focused read-only diagnosis, already a child of
the bf-39mli split. The centroid-vs-walker log (`identity.go:453-457`, `// TEMP (bf-6d2ii)`,
gated behind SPAXEL_BLE_DEBUG) was already written by a prior attempt — the work only
needed to be RUN and RECORDED. Splitting a single-conclusion read-only diagnosis into N
children would just spawn N more timeout-prone beads.

### Acceptance criteria — all 4 met

**1. Coordinates captured (SPAXEL_BLE_DEBUG=1, [BLEDBG] lines):**
- Run A — SIM_WALKERS=2 (default), FAIL: Alice triangulated `tdXY=(3.48, 1.52)`;
  nearest CSI blob `blob=5 blobXY=(4.70, 0.30)`, nBlobs=2, `hDist=1.73m`
  (√(1.22²+1.22²)=1.73 ✓), matchConf=0.143 -> REJECTED.
- Run B — SIM_WALKERS=1, PASS: Alice `tdXY=(2.82, 2.82)`; `blob=7 blobXY=(2.50, 2.30)`,
  `hDist=0.61m`, matchConf=0.714 >= 0.6 -> MATCH at t=6s.

**2. Root cause (one sentence):** With SIM_WALKERS=2, the CSI blob nearest Alice's
triangulated point is the SECOND synthetic walker's blob (parked at (4.70,0.30) in the
corner) — Alice's own location (3.48,1.52) has NO co-located CSI blob, so the matcher's
"nearest blob" is the other person's, 1.73m away. This is hypothesis #2 (forms from the
OTHER walker), NOT lag (Alice moves +x/+y, away from y=0) and NOT centroid-math/ghost-merge
(Run B proves a single walker co-locates at 0.61m; if it were lag/centroid-math Run B
would also fail).

**3. ONE minimal geometric fix — VERIFIED, not just predicted:** `SIM_WALKERS=1` for the
identity-match fixture. Post-fix gap 0.61m < 0.86m target; matchConf 0.714 clears 0.6;
run-sim-ble-match.sh PASSES. Principled for this fixture regardless: it registers exactly
ONE person (Alice) + ONE device, so the sim should emit ONE walker; the 2nd walker is
inherited from run-sim-local.sh's blob-emission stress params and is a multi-person
confound the single-person identity test does not model.

**4. No threshold loosening:** MaxBLEBlobDistance=2.0 and MinMatchConfidence=0.6 UNCHANGED
in both runs.

### Confidence math cross-check
fDist = 1-(d-0.5)/(2.0-0.5): 1.73m -> 0.18 ; 0.61m -> 0.927.
matchConf = fObs(1.0) · fNodes(4 nodes -> 0.85) · fResid(0.138->0.93 / 0.182->0.91) · fDist
= 0.143 (Run A) / 0.714 (Run B). Both match the logged values exactly.

### Handoff to child 2 (the fix)
One-line change: `SIM_WALKERS="${SIM_WALKERS:-2}"` -> `:-1` in scripts/run-sim-ble-match.sh
(~line 50). NO matcher/tracker code change; NO threshold change. Acceptance = script exits 0.
(A deeper "do 2-walker CSI blobs co-locate?" tracker investigation, if ever wanted, is a
separate bead — out of scope for this identity-chain test.)

All 4 acceptance criteria met: coords captured, root cause = wrong-walker (nearest CSI blob is the 2nd synthetic walker's, 1.73m away; Alice's own spot has no co-located blob), one minimal fix named+verified (SIM_WALKERS=1 -> gap 0.61m<0.86m, matchConf 0.714 clears 0.6), no threshold loosened. ## Context

This child confirms the same in the live app. Recent identity-blob runtime work (bf-15oi "zero errors", bf-gdfwx capstone PASS on /api/blobs) is the identity-RESOLVED path; this child is the complementary NOT-resolved path.

## Scope

- Serve the dashboard and load it (browser or headless e.g. the project's verify/run approach)

## Acceptance Criteria

issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-4do5y, 2026-07-26T09:37:18.414560377Z, author cli]
## Root cause + fix — recorded for the bf-2gmx backward-compat verification loop (bf-26sq3)

### Root cause of the FALSE PASS (blobSeen=false with a "clean" console)
The dashboard's static-file route was not registered when cfg.StaticDir (default "/dashboard", a container path) did not exist on the host. With the route unregistered, every /js/*.js and /css/* request fell through to chi's default 404 handler, which serves text/plain. The browser's strict MIME checking then refused to execute the scripts ("Refused to execute ... MIME type text/plain"). With NO JavaScript executing at all, the renderer never ran — so the identity-less code path was never exercised, the console read zero identity errors, and the capture reported blobSeen=false. That looked like backward-compat success (no errors) but was actually a false pass: nothing rendered because nothing ran.

### Fix — findDashboardDir() fallback (commit e3ef551, bf-2qywd)
- findDashboardDir() definition: mothership/cmd/mothership/main.go:288 (probes ./dashboard, ./../dashboard, /app/dashboard, then an executable-relative upward walk for the directory).
- Call site 1 — per-file dev fallback in serveEmbeddedFile: mothership/cmd/mothership/main.go:352 (staticDir := findDashboardDir()).
- Call site 2 — route-registration handler fallback: mothership/cmd/mothership/main.go:4700-4710 (when os.Stat(cfg.StaticDir) fails, fall back to findDashboardDir() at :4706, then registerDashboardStatic(r, resolvedDir) at :4710; a single WARN is emitted at :4712 only if ALL candidates are missing).

### Follow-on fix — the SyntaxErrors the MIME fix unmasked (bf-11qvm)
Once the real JS executed, 5 pre-existing parse errors surfaced and were fixed across bf-11qvm's children:
- 7f49787 — app.js: restore trailing comma after manualFrameRateCap (systemHealth reference, bf-1usoj)
- c1df213 — automation-builder.js: LHS before optional chaining (bf-15gk5)
- 5847555 — ble-panel.js: orphan close-brace / unexpected-function (bf-2hlxt)
- 9e68b4b — ambient.js / viz3d.js / sidebar-timeline: stray close-tokens (bf-2ijbq)
- a46fe1a — refresh capture -> 0 SyntaxError pageerrors (bf-lt0dk verify gate)
Result: every dashboard/js/*.js passes node --check; 0 SyntaxError lines in the re-captured console.

### Backward-compat now confirmed end-to-end (genuine, not a false pass)
Console is clean AND JS executes AND identity-less blobs render. Evidence in docs/notes/bf-4do5y-runtime-capture/:
- identity-less.summary.txt -> /live blobSeen=true msgs=157 pageErrors=0 identityHits=0
- identity-less.live.json -> renderEvidence = {viz3d:true, blobCount:2, samples:60} (non-null; 2 identity-less blobs reach the Viz3D renderer), pageErrors=[]
- identity-less.ambient.json -> renderEvidence = {canvas:true, fallbackPx:177} (the grey #6b7280 fallback color is literally on the /ambient canvas = identity-less blobs render with the fallback color)
- identity-less.api-blobs.json -> 2 blobs, both identityResolved:false (mothership serves genuine identity-less blobs)

All bf-4do5y acceptance criteria met.

The RESOLVED half of the bf-2gmx backward-compat verification now has on-disk evidence in docs/notes/bf-4do5y-runtime-capture/ (refreshed 2026-07-26 06:49, working tree):
- identity.summary.txt -> /ambient blobSeen=true msgs=12 pageErrors=0 identityHits=0 ; /live blobSeen=true msgs=136 pageErrors=0 identityHits=0
- identity.api-blobs.json -> blob ID 17 served with personName="Alice", assignedColor="#f59e0b", identityResolved=true (plus person_id/person_label/person_color/identity_confidence/identity_source=ble); a second blob (ID 18) served identityResolved=false, exercising the mixed resolved+unresolved case in one response.

issue.description:
Part of ADR-004 / bf-1447x.

The OTA path verifies a SHA-256 supplied in the same websocket message that carries the URL, which is an integrity check against corruption, not an authenticity check. There is no code signing: firmware/sdkconfig.defaults sets no CONFIG_SECURE_BOOT, no signed-app verification, and no anti-rollback. The download itself is plain HTTP (CONFIG_ESP_HTTP_CLIENT_ENABLE_HTTPS=n).

Consequence: anything that can impersonate the mothership on the node's network, or serve the firmware URL, can flash arbitrary code onto every node — and the nodes are physically distributed around a home.

Fix (staged): enable signed app verification + anti-rollback so nodes refuse unsigned or downgraded images; consider secure boot for the stronger threat model. Note enabling HTTPS on the client has a flash/RAM cost and interacts with the 4MB budget in bf-436bh, so sequence these together.
issue.notes:
Implemented Secure Boot V2, signed app verification, and anti-rollback protection for OTA firmware updates.

**Changes Made:**
1. Enabled CONFIG_SECURE_BOOT_V2=y with RSA-2048 signing (sdkconfig.defaults)
2. Enabled CONFIG_APP_ANTI_ROLLBACK=y for downgrade protection (sdkconfig.defaults)
3. Created signing infrastructure (scripts/generate-signing-key.sh, sign-firmware.sh)
4. Integrated automatic firmware signing into CMake build process
5. Added keys/ directory to .gitignore to protect private signing key
6. Documented complete security model in docs/notes/ota-security-hardening-2026-08-15.md

**Security Improvements:**
✅ Signed app verification prevents unauthorized firmware execution
✅ Anti-rollback prevents downgrade attacks
✅ Defense in depth: even with HTTP interception, unsigned images rejected

**Threats Mitigated:**
- Mothership compromise: attacker cannot flash without private key
- Network interception: attacker cannot serve unsigned firmware  
- Downgrade attacks: old, vulnerable versions refused via eFuse security version

**Remaining Work:**
- HTTPS enablement (CONFIG_ESP_HTTP_CLIENT_ENABLE_HTTPS=y) pending flash/RAM impact analysis per task note (interacts with 4MB budget in bf-436bh)
- Hardware security: burn eFuses to disable JTAG/USB for physical protection
- Production deployment requires secure signing key storage (HSM/offline)

**Deployment Notes:**
- Generate signing key: cd firmware && ./scripts/generate-signing-key.sh
- Build and sign: idf.py build (automatic when Secure Boot V2 enabled)
- Production devices: Secure Boot enabled automatically on first signed app boot
- Development boards: Can disable Secure Boot via eFuse for flexibility

Commit: 53863c8
issue.title: OTA images are unsigned and fetched over plain HTTP — anyone who can reach a node can flash it

Prefer mime.TypeByExtension or net/http FileServer/ServeFile over a custom Write that leaves Content-Type unset (some custom handlers default the unset body to text/plain).

[migrated comment from bf-1cgqe, 2026-07-08T23:54:55.719449326Z, author cli]
ROOT CAUSE FOUND (empirically verified) — the bead's original premise is a MISDIAGNOSIS.

The dashboard static handler does NOT leave Content-Type unset. It uses http.ServeFile, which sets correct MIME via mime.TypeByExtension. The real problem: the handler is never REGISTERED on the host, so every asset 404s.

REPRO (binary /tmp/spaxel-mothership, exact env from scripts/run-sim-dashboard-console.sh):
- cfg.StaticDir defaults to '/dashboard' (a container path). The harness does NOT set SPAXEL_STATIC_DIR, so on the host /dashboard is missing.
- mothership/cmd/mothership/main.go ~4601-4624 (filesystem-fallback branch): os.Stat(cfg.StaticDir) fails -> logs '[WARN] Dashboard directory not found: /dashboard' -> the r.Get("/*", http.ServeFile) handler is NEVER registered, and there is NO fallback to findDashboardDir().
- Result: curl GET /css/tokens.css -> 404, Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8 (chi's default 404 body). Chrome reports 'MIME (text/plain) is not a supported stylesheet', refuses all CSS/JS, no script runs -> blobSeen=false. THIS is the bf-4do5y FALSE PASS.

CONFIRMED FIX DIRECTION: with SPAXEL_STATIC_DIR pointed at the real dashboard/, GET returns /css/tokens.css -> 200 text/css; /js/app.js -> 200 text/javascript; / -> 200 text/html. So NO Content-Type code is needed — just fall back to findDashboardDir() (./dashboard, ./../dashboard, /app/dashboard) when the configured dir is missing.

SECOND TRAP in the original acceptance criteria: 'curl -sI' uses HEAD. The route is GET-only (r.Get), so HEAD returns 405 — a correct fix still looks broken if checked with -sI. Verify with GET: curl -s -o /dev/null -D - http://localhost:PORT/css/tokens.css

issue.description:
**Process gap — this is the bead that prevents the rest of this umbrella from happening again.** Nothing in CI compiles `firmware/`, so ~3,100 lines of ESP-IDF C accumulated with no build gate at all.

Evidence:
- `spaxel-build` (in `jedarden/declarative-config`, `k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/`) builds the mothership Docker image only. Per ADR-001 the firmware stage inside the Dockerfile is being decoupled and already emits a placeholder `.bin` on non-amd64; no path in CI asserts that the firmware actually compiles.
- `docs/notes/firmware-host-test-approach.md` records that ESP-IDF was not installed on the host that made the host-test decision, and that the decision was reasoned from source rather than from a build.
- The last recorded compile-fixing pass is commit `d7c1adc` (2026-04-14, "Port firmware/main to ESP-IDF 5.2 API") — over three months before this validation, with no gate to keep it compiling since.
- The `firmware/test/` gcc harness (the subject of ~19 currently-open beads) deliberately does **not** link `firmware/main/*.c` — by design, per its own decision record — so it provides zero protection against the firmware failing to build or failing on hardware.

Current status is better than feared: `firmware/` does compile clean under ESP-IDF v5.2 as of 2026-07-28 (5 cosmetic warnings, listed below), producing a 1,631,552-byte app that fits the 0x1F0000 factory partition with ~20% free. That is a good baseline to lock in before it rots again.

Scope:
- Add a firmware compile job to CI (either a step in `spaxel-build` or a dedicated WorkflowTemplate) that runs `idf.py set-target esp32s3 build` in `espressif/idf:v5.2` on every push touching `firmware/`. Note that ADR-001 already calls for building the firmware once on an amd64 runner and publishing it as a versioned artifact — this bead is the natural place to land that build step, so coordinate rather than duplicate.
- Fail the build on compile error, and assert the app binary still fits the factory partition (`check_sizes.py` already does this — surface it as a gate, not just log output).
- Treat warnings as a tracked baseline. The 5 current warnings are: unused `last_state_change` (`main.c:185`), unused `save_nvs_rate` (`main.c:168`), unused `save_nvs_role` (`main.c:154`), unused `broadcast_mac` (`csi.c:281`), and deprecated `esp_bluedroid_init` (`ble.c:59`). Clean these up so the baseline is zero, then consider `-Werror`.
- Do not gate on flashing/hardware in CI — there is no board attached to the CI cluster. Hardware validation stays manual (see the bench flashing-procedure bead) until a self-hosted runner with a board exists.

Acceptance criteria:
- A push touching `firmware/` triggers a CI job that compiles the ESP32-S3 target and fails on any compile error.
- A deliberately introduced compile error is confirmed to fail that job.
- Binary-size-vs-partition is a hard gate.
- The 5 known warnings are resolved and the build is warning-clean.
issue.notes: Implemented and pushed: Spaxel 3723e37 adds -Werror firmware component compilation, removes the five known unused/deprecated warnings, fixes the current ESP-IDF format/Kconfig warnings, and adds the missing transport abstraction sources required by the committed provisioning refactor. Declarative-config e0c52576 adds an explicit check_sizes.py app-partition hard gate to the existing espressif/idf:v5.2 firmware-build step; the existing Sensor path filter fails open for firmware/ pushes and ignores docs-only pushes. Verified locally in espressif/idf:v5.2: idf.py set-target esp32s3 build passed with no warnings; app 0x19f7b0 vs 0x1f0000 slots (16% free); explicit check_sizes.py passed. A deliberate syntax error failed the ESP-IDF build (status 2); a deliberate 1-byte oversize app failed check_sizes.py (status 1). firmware/test make passed; go vet passed. Full go test was attempted but remains red in unrelated pre-existing shared-checkout edits under mothership/internal/recording and two API tests; those changes were preserved unstaged. Both pushed revisions are visible on the GitHub mirror.
issue.title: Add firmware compile gate to CI — nothing has ever built firmware/, which is why these defects went unseen

issue.description:
## Background

The 3D scene is great for spatial context but poor for bulk fleet management tasks. With 6+ nodes, finding a specific node in the 3D view, checking its firmware version, and triggering an update involves hunting through the scene. The fleet status page provides a flat table view of all nodes with their key metrics and inline actions — the same information you would find in a server management panel, adapted for ESP32 nodes. It complements the 3D view rather than replacing it.

## Fleet Status Table

New dashboard route: /fleet

The page layout:
- Page header: "Fleet Status" title, total node count, online count, "Update All" button, "Download report" button
- Filter and sort bar (below header)
- Fleet table (main content)

Table columns:
1. Checkbox (for multi-select)
2. Label (editable inline on double-click)
3. MAC address (truncated, full on hover tooltip)
4. Status: coloured dot + text. "Online" (green) / "Offline" (red) / "Updating" (yellow spinner)
5. Firmware version: current version string. If a newer version is in the firmware manifest: version displayed in amber with an "→ {new_version}" indicator and an "Update" action badge.
6. Uptime: formatted as "3d 4h 12m". Only valid when online.
7. Current role: TX / RX / TX-RX / Passive. Small badge.
8. Signal health: composite health score for this node's links as a small colour bar (green → red)
9. Packet rate: "{actual} / {configured} Hz" as a fraction. Colour-coded: > 90% = green, 70-90% = amber, < 70% = red.
10. Temperature: from health message. Shown as "{N}°C" or "--" if not reported. Alert colour if > 75°C.
11. Actions column: [Locate] [OTA] [...more] buttons

The table rows are clickable (full row click = fly 3D camera to that node's position). Only clicking action buttons or the checkbox should not trigger the row fly-to.

## Inline Label Edit

Double-clicking the label cell makes it inline-editable:
- Input field replaces the text
- Enter to confirm, Escape to cancel
- Blur (click outside) to confirm
- On confirm: PATCH /api/nodes/{mac}/label with the new label. Update the display.
- Validation: max 32 characters, no control characters.

## Action Buttons

"Locate" (flash LED): sends a downstream command {"type":"identify"} to the node via WebSocket. The node flashes its onboard LED rapidly for 5 seconds. The button shows a spinner while the command is in-flight, then a brief green checkmark.

"OTA" (firmware update): available only if the node's firmware version != latest in the manifest. Clicking shows a confirmation tooltip: "Update Node [label] from v{current} to v{latest}? [Confirm] [Cancel]". On confirm: POST /api/nodes/{mac}/ota. The node's row shows "Updating" status and a progress bar (populated from ota_status WebSocket messages for this node).

"More actions" (... button): dropdown with: "Re-assign role", "View health history", "View event history", "Remove from fleet". Each with an appropriate icon.

## Bulk Actions

Checkbox column allows multi-selecting rows. When any row is selected, a bulk-actions bar slides in above the table:
- "Update {N} selected to latest firmware" — confirms and triggers OTA for all selected nodes in sequence (with 30s stagger)
- "Re-assign roles" — opens the role optimiser with the selected nodes included
- "Remove {N} from fleet" — confirmation required: lists the nodes to be removed

Deselect all: "Clear selection" button in the bulk actions bar, or uncheck all checkboxes.

## Camera Fly-To

Clicking a table row (non-action click) triggers a smooth camera fly-to the node's position in the expert mode 3D view. The fleet page and expert mode are on different routes, so this requires:
1. Store the target node MAC in localStorage or URL parameter ("?highlight={mac}")
2. Redirect to the expert mode route / (or open expert mode in a second tab)
3. On load, if ?highlight={mac} parameter is present, fly camera to that node's position

Alternatively: if the fleet page is opened alongside the expert mode in a split-pane layout (future enhancement), coordinate via a shared state store. For Phase 9, the redirect approach is sufficient.

## Sorting and Filtering

Column header click: sort by that column. First click = ascending, second = descending. Sort state shown with a small arrow indicator.

Filter row (below column headers, toggle-able with a "Filter" button):
- Label / MAC: text input, filters rows containing the substring
- Status: dropdown "All / Online / Offline"
- Firmware: dropdown "All / Outdated only"
- Role: multi-select dropdown "All / TX / RX / TX-RX / Passive"

Active filters: shown as chips above the table with individual dismiss buttons. "Clear all filters" link.

## Download Report

"Download report" button: exports the current fleet table (including all filters) as a CSV file. Columns: MAC, label, status, firmware_version, uptime_s, role, health_score, packet_rate_hz, temperature_c, last_seen.

Implemented as a client-side CSV generation from the current table data (no API call needed if data is cached in the dashboard state). Use Blob + URL.createObjectURL for download.

## REST API

GET /api/fleet: returns all provisioned nodes with full details (same as GET /api/nodes but with more fields: uptime, firmware_version, temperature, health_score, packet_rate).
PATCH /api/nodes/{mac}/label: update label
POST /api/nodes/{mac}/locate: send identify command
POST /api/nodes/{mac}/role: assign new role
DELETE /api/nodes/{mac}: remove from fleet (disconnects and archives)

## Files to Create or Modify

- dashboard/fleet.html: fleet page HTML shell
- dashboard/js/fleet.js: table rendering, sorting, filtering, bulk actions, inline edit
- dashboard/css/fleet.css: fleet page styles
- mothership/internal/dashboard/routes.go: fleet-specific API routes, /fleet HTML route

## Tests

- Test fleet table renders correctly with mock data: 4 nodes, verify all columns populated
- Test inline label edit: double-click cell, type new label, Enter -> PATCH API called with correct body
- Test bulk selection: check 3 nodes, verify bulk actions bar appears with correct count
- Test bulk OTA triggers OTA for all 3 selected nodes
- Test sorting: click "Firmware version" header -> rows sorted ascending by version string
- Test filter: enter "living" in label filter -> only rows matching "living" visible
- Test camera fly-to: clicking a row stores MAC in localStorage and redirects to expert mode with ?highlight parameter
- Test CSV download: verify blob is created with correct headers and values

## Acceptance Criteria

- Fleet page loads with all nodes and their current metrics
- Inline label edit saves correctly to the API and updates the display
- Bulk OTA fires for all selected nodes with correct stagger
- Sorting and filtering work correctly for all columns
- Camera fly-to positions the 3D view correctly on the selected node after redirect
- CSV download contains correct headers and all fleet data
- Tests pass

issue.close_reason: Shipped 5adf94e: seed semver-named app-only OTA firmware, isolate merged serial-flash image, prevent unversioned files becoming latest, and verify built image/API behavior.
issue.description:
Found 2026-08-07 on the bench rig while inspecting why the fleet page dangled an update at a node.

Dockerfile builds a MERGED full-flash image and seeds it as the OTA payload:

  Dockerfile:67-74   esptool merge_bin --output build/spaxel-firmware-merged.bin \
                       0x0 bootloader.bin  0x8000 partition-table.bin \
                       0x10000 ota_data_initial.bin  0x20000 spaxel-firmware.bin
  Dockerfile:135     COPY --from=firmware-builder .../spaxel-firmware-merged.bin /firmware/spaxel-firmware.bin

The mothership copies /firmware/*.bin into its firmware store on first run and serves those files as OTA payloads. Two problems, both still present on main:

1) WRONG IMAGE TYPE. An OTA client writes the payload into an app partition, so the payload must be the app-only binary (build/spaxel-firmware.bin). A merged image is only valid written to flash offset 0 -- it leads with the bootloader, then the partition table, then otadata. Serving it as OTA puts a bootloader at the start of an app slot. Verified on the running container's seed: the app descriptor sits at file offset 0x10020 (i.e. app at 0x10000, the pre-A/B factory offset for that vintage), NOT at byte 0 where an OTA payload's must be. Current Dockerfile merges the app at 0x20000 instead, so the exact offset moved, but it is a merged image either way.

2) UNVERSIONED FILENAME -> NONSENSE VERSION, MARKED LATEST. The COPY renames it to the version-less spaxel-firmware.bin, so the store parses the version out of the filename and records the literal string:

  GET /api/firmware ->
  {filename: spaxel-firmware.bin, version: "spaxel-firmware", is_latest: true, size_bytes: 1696480}

is_latest=true means every connected node is shown an available update to a non-semver "version". The fleet dashboard renders it as '0.2.17 -> spaxel-firmware' with Update All one click away. The image's own embedded app version is the literal string '1' (the PROJECT_VERSION reassignment trap of bf-556tl, which 0.1.358 predates).

Impact: pressing Update All / a per-node update against a fresh mothership serves a malformed OTA payload. Best case the node rejects it at esp_ota_end() validation and reports write_failed; either way it churns the node, and the store keeps advertising the bogus update forever. Currently latent because auto_update_enabled=False by default -- an operator click is required.

Suggested fix: seed the app-only artifact under a versioned filename, e.g. COPY build/spaxel-firmware.bin to /firmware/spaxel-firmware-${VERSION}.bin, so GetByVersion/GetByFilename resolve properly and is_latest reflects a real semver. Keep the merged image as a separate serial-flash artifact if it is wanted for first-flash, but it must not land in the OTA store.
issue.title: Seeded OTA firmware is a merged full-flash image under an unversioned filename — store advertises bogus 'latest' to every node

issue.description:
Split-child 2 of 4 for parent bf-38e9. Depends on child 1 (bf-52k2).

GOAL: parity — exactly one observable line per test on BOTH paths, both using the SAME neutral marker family (no PASS/FAIL on either). The committed direct path currently prints an outcome label:

    g_tests[i].fn();
    printf("PASS: %s\n", g_tests[i].name);
    passed++;

Replace "PASS: %s" with the matching neutral marker family chosen in child 1, e.g.:

    printf("RUN: %s\n", g_tests[i].name);

so a passing test prints "RUN: <name>" and a failing test (child 1) prints "RUN: <name> (assertion failed)". Keep the internal passed++ counter — it feeds the summary line, not the per-test output, so it is not an "observable label".

After this child, NEITHER branch emits PASS/FAIL; each test emits exactly one neutral line.

Acceptance criteria:
- Direct path prints exactly one neutral marker naming the test, same family as child 1's else-branch marker.
- Neither the direct nor the else branch contains a PASS or FAIL token.
- passed/failed counters and g_failure_count accounting are unchanged.
- Compiles cleanly: gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra.

issue.description:
State as of 2026-08-07 ~11:25 EDT, bench rig, node 50:78:7D:1A:3D:C8.

WHAT IS DONE (all committed and deployed):
 - Firmware supports wss:// + CA-bundle validation for both the websocket and the OTA http client (spaxel 4393692). Port 443 selects TLS. Cost +65,968 bytes, 17% of the app partition still free.
 - Production is on 0.2.19 with SPAXEL_ADVERTISED_BASE_URL=https://spaxel.ardenone.com (declarative-config; note a late CI run reverted the pin to 0.2.18 once and it had to be re-pinned).
 - Production /ws/node verified reachable and NOT behind OAuth: an HTTP/1.1 upgrade returns 101 Switching Protocols through Cloudflare. (Over HTTP/2 it returns 400 -- test with --http1.1.)
 - The bench AP now has internet: iptables MASQUERADE for 192.168.50.0/24 out enp0s25, FORWARD rules both ways, and dhcp-option=6,1.1.1.1,8.8.8.8 added to dnsmasq (it runs port=0, DHCP-only, so clients previously had NO resolver). All imperative and NOT persistent across a bench reboot.
 - NVS was rewritten for production: ms_ip/ms_ip_prov=spaxel.ardenone.com, ms_port=443, node_token minted from prod's own /api/provision.
 - Console now survives the provisioning window (provision_release_console() calls esp_vfs_usb_serial_jtag_use_nonblocking() BEFORE uninstalling the driver). This is what finally made wifi_init() logs visible.

WHERE IT STOPPED:
 - Console showed the node reaching wifi_init, then 'WiFi disconnected' / 'WiFi failed (attempt 1)' ~4s after STA start.
 - conntrack confirmed the node DID resolve spaxel.ardenone.com (172.67.219.132) and open repeated TCP connections to port 443, all short-lived (TIME_WAIT churn) -- so TLS was being attempted and not completing. It also briefly held a TCP session to bench:8080 (mDNS discovery finding the bench mothership, which competes on the same LAN).
 - Node is now unreachable: 100% ping loss, zero conntrack entries, no DHCP renewal.
 - esptool cannot recover it: every connect fails 'A serial exception error occurred: Write timeout'. That is exactly bf-4z6wh, which the handoff notes only a PHYSICAL USB REPLUG clears. Two retries confirmed.

NEXT STEPS (needs someone at the bench):
 1. Physically unplug/replug the ESP32-S3 USB cable. That clears the esptool wedge and power-cycles the node.
 2. Re-check whether it connects to prod on its own -- the NVS already points there.
 3. If TLS still fails, the prime suspect is CLOCK: mbedTLS cert validation rejects a chain when the wall clock is wrong, and this node has historically never had working NTP (the bench AP had no internet until today). Confirm NTP sync succeeds now before blaming the TLS stack. Heap during handshake is the second suspect (WiFi + BLE + CSI + mbedTLS on one ESP32-S3).
 4. Consider stopping the bench mothership or setting SPAXEL_MDNS_ENABLED=false on it while the node is meant to be on production -- otherwise mDNS discovery keeps offering it a closer, plaintext mothership.
